new_roles.title: Senior Director, Merchandise Manufacturing & Sourcing
new_roles.description:
**Job Description:**
====================

NOTE: This role is based in New York City and encourages a minimum of two days per week in the SoHo office. Some roles or teams may require additional in-office attendance if the essential functions of the role require it.

THE OPPORTUNITY

The Senior Director, Merchandise Manufacturing & Strategic Sourcing is a key global leadership role responsible for the strategic sourcing, manufacturing, commercialization, and production execution of Scholastic's merchandise portfolio supporting Book Fairs, Book Clubs, Trade Publishing, Discovery Fairs, and future consumer product initiatives.

Reporting directly to the SVP Manufacturing who is responsible for Global Supply Chain and Procurement, this position serves as the critical bridge between Product Development, Editorial, Design, Category Management, Publishing, and global manufacturing partners.

This leader partners with internal stakeholders from the earliest stages of product ideation, providing expertise in product engineering, sourcing strategy, manufacturing capabilities, material selection, cost optimization, and production feasibility. The objective is to transform creative concepts into high-quality, innovative products that deliver exceptional customer experiences while achieving aggressive cost, quality, and speed-to-market objectives.

The role oversees a global sourcing portfolio exceeding $200 million annually and leads an international team of approximately 12 professionals located across the United States and India. The position may be based in the United States, China, or India and requires extensive collaboration with domestic and international suppliers and manufacturing partners.

RESPONSIBILITIES

**Product Development, Ideation & Publishing Partnership**

* Serve as a strategic partner to Publishing, Editorial, Design, Category Management, Book Fairs, Book Clubs, Trade, and other stakeholders to translate creative concepts and intellectual property into compelling, manufacturable products.
* Engage early in product ideation, bringing manufacturing and sourcing expertise to decisions around materials, formats, construction, packaging, features, price points, and production methods.
* Proactively introduce new product concepts, materials, manufacturing capabilities, and supplier innovations that expand Scholastic's product opportunities.
* Partner throughout the development cycle from concept, specification, prototyping, sampling, and costing through pproval and production.
* Challenge and improve concepts where appropriate to enhance consumer appeal, quality, manufacturability, sustainability, speed, and cost.

**Consumer Products & Sourcing Strategy**

* Lead development of the sourcing and manufacturing strategy supporting Scholastic's expanding consumer-products and merchandise initiatives.
* Partner with business and publishing leadership to identify new product categories and opportunities across Book Fairs, Discovery Fairs, retail, e-commerce, licensing, and other emerging channels.
* Develop category sourcing strategies addressing manufacturing regions, supplier capabilities, cost, lead times, minimum quantities, tooling, quality, and supply-chain risk.
* Build a proactive pipeline of product ideas and manufacturing capabilities that can be regularly presented to internal stakeholders.
* Maintain awareness of consumer trends, emerging categories, materials, and manufacturing technologies and translate those insights into actionable product opportunities.

**Global Vendor Development & Innovation**

* Proactively identify and develop innovative manufacturers and product-development partners, particularly those offering engineering expertise, rapid prototyping, unique materials, creative capabilities, and new manufacturing technologies.
* Develop suppliers that can function as extensions of Scholastic's product-development organization, proactively bringing forward new concepts and capabilities.
* Continuously evaluate the supplier portfolio to improve competitiveness, increase speed, diversify supply, reduce risk, and enable entry into new categories.

**Global Sourcing, Cost & Operational Leadership**

* Develop and execute a comprehensive global sourcing strategy supporting more than $200 million in annual product expense.
* Establish sourcing roadmaps and supplier-diversification strategies that anticipate future business requirements and reduce dependency on individual suppliers or regions.
* Ensure products consistently meet expectations for quality, safety, regulatory compliance, sustainability, cost, and on-time delivery.

**Supplier Engagement & Global Travel**

* Maintain direct senior-level engagement with strategic manufacturing partners and regularly visit supplier facilities to evaluate capabilities, innovation, quality, capacity, and operational performance.
* Significant international travel is expected, with consistent travel to Asia, particularly China and India, as well as other global sourcing markets as required.
* Use supplier visits as product-development and innovation opportunities to identify new materials, manufacturing processes, capabilities, and product concepts for Scholastic.
* Participate in relevant trade shows, sourcing events, and supplier innovation sessions to identify emerging capabilities and potential partners.

**Organizational Leadership**

* Lead and develop a global organization of approximately 12 professionals across the United States and India.
* Build a culture combining sourcing discipline with creativity, product knowledge, commercial thinking, and an entrepreneurial approach to product development.
* Develop team capabilities in product ideation, product development, supplier innovation, value engineering, and strategic sourcing.
* Build strong partnerships across Publishing, Editorial, Design, Category Management, Supply Chain, Finance, and senior leadership, positioning the organization as a strategic product-development partner.

**Key Measures of Success**

Success will be measured through product development and innovation, cost per unit and total landed-cost, speed to market, supplier innovation and diversification, quality and compliance, on-time performance.

**About Scholastic**

For more than 100 years, Scholastic Corporation (NASDAQ: SCHL) has been meeting children where they are – at school, at home and in their communities – by creating quality content and experiences, all beginning with literacy. Scholastic delivers stories, characters, and learning moments that empower all kids to become lifelong readers and learners through bestselling children’s books, literacy- and knowledge-building resources for schools including classroom magazines, and award-winning, entertaining children's media. As the world's largest publisher and distributor of children's books through school-based book clubs and book fairs, classroom libraries, school and public libraries, retail, and online, and with a global reach into more than 135 countries, Scholastic encourages the personal and intellectual growth of all children, while nurturing a lifelong relationship with reading, themselves, and the world around them. Learn more at www.scholastic.com.

Some benefits that we offer:

 

* Full suite of health and wellness benefits (including a $0 deductible Medical Plan)
* Retirement Savings Plan 401(k) with options for both Roth and Traditional Contributions
* Tuition-Free programs for undergraduate and graduate degrees
* Generous Parental Leave Program
* Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) with opportunity for discounted stock at a 15% discount

Thank you for your consideration in choosing Scholastic.

new_roles.title: Director of Operations
new_roles.description:
Location:

Garden City, NY, US, 11530

Business Unit: Treitler FMH

Posting Date: Nov 20, 2026

Job Description:

**Position Summary:**

The Director of Operations is responsible for leading Hughes-Treitler operations to achieve business objectives related to safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, and customer satisfaction. This hands-on leadership role provides strategic and day-to-day direction for manufacturing, materials, and operational excellence while ensuring the organization has the talent, capacity, processes, and resources required to support current demand and business growth. The Director establishes operating plans, drives accountability, builds organizational capability, and leads continuous improvement initiatives that improve performance, expand capacity, control costs, and strengthen customer responsiveness.

 
 

**Supervisory Responsibilties:**

The position has direct reports but must be able to work in partnership with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain and Production in support of the departmental objectives. 



**Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Lead and develop Operations teams to effectively support day-to-day execution, strategic business objectives, customer requirements, and growth plans.
* Establish operating strategies, objectives, budgets, capital requirements, material plans, labor requirements, and organizational priorities aligned with customer and business needs.
* Ensure the organization is structured and staffed with the talent, resources, and capabilities needed to meet customer quality, technical, delivery, and turnaround-time expectations.
* Partner with business leadership to achieve key performance indicators, including safety, quality, on-time delivery, throughput, backlog reduction, customer lead time, productivity, labor utilization, cost, and profitability.
* Lead the development and execution of the site Lean and Operational Excellence roadmap, using Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, 5S, TPM, SIOP and daily management practices to improve flow, yield, cycle time, productivity, and cost performance.
* Establish and monitor operating standards, performance metrics, and management routines that drive accountability, timely problem-solving, and sustained results.
* Drive capacity planning and expansion initiatives, including capital equipment, automation, facility, tooling, staffing, and process investments required to support business growth.
* Manage operating expenses and capital investments in accordance with approved budgets; identify and execute cost-reduction and productivity opportunities.
* Ensure effective planning and control of materials, inventory, suppliers, production schedules, and labor resources to support quality, cost, and delivery commitments.
* Collaborate with Quality, Engineering, Sales, Finance, and other cross-functional partners to resolve operational issues, support new product introductions, strengthen manufacturability, and meet customer requirements.
* Provide leadership for robust root cause analysis, corrective actions, and continuous improvement activities related to safety, quality, delivery, cost, and customer performance.
* Participate in the development and execution of the business strategy and translate strategic priorities into actionable operating plans and measurable objectives.
* Support commercial and customer-facing activities, including operational reviews, pricing and capacity analyses, customer visits, and performance presentations.
* Recruit, develop, coach, and retain operations talent through performance management, career development, succession planning, cross-training, and ongoing capability building.
* Foster a culture of accountability, employee engagement, collaboration, innovation, safety, and continuous improvement across the organization.
* Author annual performance reviews and develop continuing education and advancement paths for entire department.
* Demonstrate the ability and willingness to use AI tools appropriately to improve productivity, decision-making, work quality, and cost performance, including identifying suitable use cases and critically evaluating AI-generated outputs.
 

**Required Skills and Abilities:**

* Strong leadership, project management, analytical, problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
* Demonstrated success leading manufacturing operations and continuous improvement initiatives in a complex manufacturing environment.
* Proficiency with Lean, Six Sigma, 5S, Kaizen, TPM, and other continuous improvement methodologies.
* Ability to establish performance metrics, analyze operating data, prioritize competing demands, and drive accountability for results.
* Proven ability to lead change, manage multiple complex initiatives, and meet critical deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
* Exceptional interpersonal, written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to build effective work relationships.
* Strong customer orientation and demonstrated ability to balance customer requirements with operational, financial, and organizational priorities.
* Ability to work effectively under pressure, exercise sound judgment, and maintain a hands-on leadership presence across the operation.
* Proficiency with enterprise resource planning and manufacturing systems; experience with SIOP or related planning processes preferred.
* Demonstrated history of successful change management and implementation of operational excellence improvements.
* Strong interpersonal, leadership and organizational skills and the ability to communicate with all levels of the organization from the production floor to the executive office.
* Willingness to work a flexible schedule and travel as needed to support business requirements.
 

**Education and Experience:**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain, Business, or another related technical discipline required; MBA or other relevant advanced degree preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive manufacturing operations leadership experience in a low-volume/high-mix, build-to-order, or engineered-products environment; experience in aerospace, defense, metal-forming, precision machining, brazing, welding, or another highly regulated industry preferred.
* Demonstrated experience leading salaried and hourly employees.
* Demonstrated experience leading Lean Manufacturing, Operational Excellence, and continuous improvement programs with measurable results.
* Demonstrated experience driving operational planning, capital and capacity expansion, production and materials management, cost optimization, organizational improvements, and customer-facing operational reviews.

**Other**

* Due to the nature of Hughes-Treitler's programs and products, applicants must have the legal right to work in the US and additionally must be legally authorized to access export-controlled information and source code.

**Physical Requirements:**

* None

**Compensation**
----------------

Employee Type: Salaried

Currency: USD

Salary Minimum: 200,000

Salary Maximum: 225,000

Incentive: No

Disclaimer: Where a specific pay range is noted, it is a good faith estimate at the time of this posting. The actual salary offered will be based on experience, skills, qualifications, market / business considerations, and geographic location.

AMETEK is committed to making a safer, sustainable, and more productive world a reality. We use differentiated technology solutions to solve our customers’ most complex challenges. We employ 22,000 colleagues, in 35 countries, that are grounded by our core values: Ethics and Integrity, Respect for the Individual, Inclusion, Teamwork, and Social Responsibility. AMETEK is a component of the S&P 500. Visit https://www.ametek.com/careers for more information.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a veteran, and basis of disability or any other federal, state or local protected class. Individuals who need a reasonable accommodation because of a disability for any part of the employment process should call 1 (866) 263-8359.

new_roles.description:
Description:

**Join Weiss-Aug – A Leader in Precision Manufacturing and Innovation**

Be part of a company that’s shaping the future of manufacturing where your ideas, skills, and passion matter.

Weiss-Aug, is a leading provider of advanced manufacturing and engineering solutions with advanced facilities across the U.S. and Mexico for over 50 years.

**Why Join Us?**

At Weiss-Aug we are driven by a commitment to excellence, innovation, and continuous improvement. As a recognized leader in the industrial and commercial sectors, specializing in high-volume metal stamping, thermoplastic molding, and value-added assembly solutions for the medical, aerospace & defense, automotive, interconnect, telecommunications and consumer goods industries, we take pride in cultivating a collaborative and forward-thinking work environment.

We're currently seeking a passionate and skilled ***Director of Operations*** to join our team and contribute to our mission of delivering high-quality, engineered solutions to our customers worldwide. In this role you will be responsible for planning and directing line management and related manufacturing support activities including manufacturing floor inspection, manufacturing engineering, materials management and safety/environmental engineering. Establishes and implements manufacturing policies, controls and procedures to further the company's interest in efficiently producing quality products. Contributes to achievement of sales objectives and to the establishment. Prepares or assists in the annual budgets for all departments and is responsible for profit and loss of the division. Manages Manufacturing Managers of Molding and Stamping, Purchasing, Warehouse, Manufacturing Engineering, Customer Service/Planning.

**Responsibilities**

* Management of manufacturing operations. Plans, schedules, organizes, and staffs manufacturing and manufacturing support functions. Assures that all groups within manufacturing organization are properly staffed and coordinated; and that personnel in each group are properly qualified, directed and trained to perform their duties effectively.
* Interprets company sales forecasts and shop orders and establishes accurate manufacturing plans to assure that our customers' requirements are met, that is, defect free product on time.
* Coordinates with Engineering, Sales and new product development engineering to maintain an awareness of current and future product plans.
* Develops and manages material control, manufacturing control, production scheduling, and planning systems to assure achievement of output schedules which will meet company sales requirements.
* Maintains material and parts inventories which are adequate to ensure the fulfillment of production schedules with minimum inventory expense.
* Plans and develops manufacturing facilities and equipment for efficient production of products.
* Works with tooling/engineering to investigate product quality and manufacturing problems and determine the most cost-efficient solutions.
* Develops and assists with the annual budget of all departments; develops and is responsible for all standard costs. Recommends pricing based on the profit objective of the company. Is responsible for the profit and loss of the division.
* Meets or exceeds all TQM measurements as agreed upon annually.
* Is a member of the executive team and steering team which are responsible for the development of company policies and plans.
* Participates with other top managers in the development of company business policies as needed.

Requirements:

* Bachelor's degree Mechanical or Industrial Engineering.
* 8-10 years precision manufacturing experience including some experience in molding. (10 years in management role).
* Strong leadership skills.
* Should have a working knowledge of computerized manufacturing systems.

This position is at our ***East Hanover, NJ*** location.

Pay Range: $150,000 - $180,000

**Other Benefits Include**

* Medical, Dental and Vision
* 401 (k) with company match
* Holiday, Vacation and Sick Time
* Tuition Reimbursement
* Health Savings Accounts (HSA)
* Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
* Cigna Wellness Incentive Program
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Short Term Disability
* Group Life and Accidental Insurance
* Sun Life – Accident, Critical Illness, and Hospital Indemnity Insurance
* Smoking Cessation Program
* Pet Insurance

**US Pay Transparency**

The base salary for this role will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, experience, and internal consistency.

If your salary requirements exceed the advertised range and you remain interested in Weiss-Aug, we encourage you to apply.

Weiss-Aug is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. Applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other characteristics protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

new_roles.title: Director, Quality GxP Vendor Management & Audit Programs
new_roles.description:
Description:

**The Company:**

This publicly held clinical-stage biotechnology company is focused on developing treatments for patients suffering from complex rare diseases using its novel cell penetrating peptide technology platform. Their lead product candidate, nomlabofusp, is a subcutaneously administered, recombinant fusion protein intended to deliver human frataxin (FXN), an essential protein to the mitochondria of patients with Friedreich’s ataxia. Friedreich’s ataxia is a rare, progressive, and fatal disease in which patients are unable to produce sufficient FXN due to a genetic abnormality.

The company has 80 employees and has assembled an experienced management team, each of whom has over 20 years of pharmaceutical industry experience. The management team, employees, and consultants have significant expertise in discovery, nonclinical and clinical development, regulatory affairs, commercialization, and the development of manufacturing processes utilizing good manufacturing practices (GMPs).

The company’s strategy is to become a leader in the treatment of rare diseases by leveraging their technology platform and applying their team’s know-how and expertise to the development of CTI-1601 and other future pipeline programs. They are best characterized by entrepreneurial and scientific leadership and a participatory workforce committed to success.

**Position Summary:**

The Director, GxP Vendor Management is responsible for leading Larimar’s GxP vendor management and audit programs and collaborating with key functional area stakeholders to ensure vendors are selected, qualified, managed and overseen in compliance with Larimar and regulatory requirements. This role owns the full vendor lifecycle and will shape the program’s strategy as Larimar seeks BLA approval, progresses with Phase 3 trial and plans for commercialization.

**Job Responsibilities:**

* Lead and implement the strategic direction of the vendor management and audit programs at Larimar.
* Own the risk-based vendor qualification framework, including risk tiering and minimum oversight expectations for each tier, and manage day-to-day qualification activities through vendor audit and assessment, qualification, approval and filing of vendor-related qualification documentation.
* Maintain an approved vendor list and a master tracker of all GxP vendors (current, historic, and planned) as the single source of truth for vendor qualification/requalification, audit, and Quality Agreements.
* Partner with functional areas to develop and oversee execution of the risk-based annual external audit plan, including auditor assignments, audit tracking, follow up of audit responses and CAPAs, and filing of audit documentation.
* Manage the internal audit program including development and execution of internal audit plan to adequately assess Larimar’s internal processes.
* Manage the Quality Agreement program, including development and maintenance of Quality Agreements, and partner with Legal and functional areas to ensure Quality Agreements are in place and current with applicable vendors.
* Partner with functional areas to develop, review and maintain risk-based vendor oversight plans, including expectations for KPIs; governance meetings; issue escalation; oversight activities, frequency, responsibility, and documentation requirements; and verification that vendors and their subcontractors use qualified personnel.
* Conduct training on vendor management and audit programs to ensure functional areas understand and appropriately execute their responsibilities.
* Partner with functional areas to identify vendor deviations to assess issues potentially impacting the vendor qualification status or required oversight.
* Develop Vendor Management metrics, analyze vendor performance and compliance trends, and lead a periodic cross-functional vendor review that feeds into Quality Management Review.
* Ensure inspection readiness in the vendor management function and assist functional areas with readiness related to selection, qualification, management and oversight of their vendors.
* Evaluate and implement electronic vendor management systems, as applicable.

Requirements:

**Qualifications:**

* BS/BA in a life science or related field, or equivalent industry experience.
* 10+ years’ experience in the Pharmaceutical/Biotechnology industry, including at least 5 years leading vendor management/audit programs in a GxP environment.
* Expert knowledge of FDA, EMA, MHRA and ICH GxP regulations and guidelines, including ICH E6(R3) expectations for sponsor oversight of service providers.
* Strong GxP foundation associated with vendor oversight.
* Demonstrated experience planning and managing GxP vendor and internal audits, including follow up of audit responses and CAPAs.
* Experience developing and negotiating Quality Agreements with CROs, laboratories and other GxP service providers.
* Proficient with Veeva Systems, including Veeva Vault QualityDocs, desirable.
* Experience applying risk-based approaches to vendor tiering and oversight.
* Strong communication skills with all levels of the organization and external vendors, and the ability to influence functional areas without direct authority.
* Excellent organizational skills, analytical and problem-solving abilities, and strong verbal and writing skills.

**Benefits:**

Larimar Therapeutics offers all employees incentive stock options, a comprehensive benefits plan including 401K, and a flexible PTO policy.

***Equal Opportunity Employment***

*We are committed to equal-employment principles, and we recognize the value of committed employees who feel they are being treated in an equitable and professional manner. We strive to find ways to attract, develop and retain the talent needed to meet business objectives, and to recruit and employ highly qualified individuals representing the diverse communities in which we live.*

*Employment policies and decisions on employment and promotion are based on merit, qualifications, performance, and business needs. The decisions and criteria governing the employment relationship with all employees are made in a non-discriminatory manner—without regard to age, race, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth or medical condition related to pregnancy or childbirth), gender identity or expression, religion, physical or mental disability, medical condition, legally protected genetic information, marital status, veteran status, military status, sexual orientation, or any other factor determined to be an unlawful basis for such decisions by federal, state, or local statutes.*

new_roles.title: Senior Director, Automation & New Process Engineering
new_roles.description:
**Job Description:**

**Position Overview**
---------------------

TransMedics is seeking a **Senior Director of Automation and New Process Engineering** to lead a critical transformation within our R&D and Engineering organization. This highly visible leadership position will oversee Automation, New Product Introduction (NPI), and Sustaining Engineering, driving engineering innovation, manufacturing excellence, and operational scalability.

**This is a build role, not a maintain role.**

As TransMedics continues its rapid growth, we need a strategic, hands-on engineering leader who can develop and execute a multi-year transformation roadmap while remaining closely connected to day-to-day manufacturing operations.

The ideal candidate combines deep technical expertise in automation and advanced manufacturing with proven experience building high-performing engineering organizations. This leader will drive improvements in product quality, reliability, manufacturing efficiency, and scalability while developing the engineering talent needed to support our continued growth.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

**Engineering Leadership & Organizational Development**

* Lead the Automation, New Product Introduction, and Sustaining Engineering organizations.
* Develop and execute a multi-year engineering transformation strategy aligned with business growth.
* Build, mentor, and develop high-performing, multidisciplinary engineering teams.
* Establish organizational structures, processes, and capabilities to support long-term scalability.
* Oversee performance management, professional development, and engineering resource planning.

**Automation & Advanced Manufacturing**

* Drive the implementation of advanced automation, robotics, and innovative manufacturing technologies.
* Lead automation initiatives across multiple manufacturing lines to improve quality, efficiency, and throughput.
* Identify opportunities to modernize manufacturing processes, systems, and infrastructure.
* Establish scalable, reliable, and cost-effective manufacturing solutions.

**New Product Introduction & Sustaining Engineering**

* Provide strategic leadership for NPI engineering and manufacturing process development.
* Ensure successful transitions from product development into scalable manufacturing.
* Lead sustaining engineering initiatives to improve existing products and manufacturing processes.
* Partner with cross-functional teams to resolve complex technical challenges and support product launches.
* Maintain a hands-on approach to troubleshooting manufacturing issues and addressing production or launch risks.

**Design for Excellence (DfX)**

* Champion Design for Excellence (DfX), including Design for Manufacturability (DFM), throughout the product development lifecycle.
* Drive product and process simplification, including part-count reduction.
* Improve product reliability, manufacturing efficiency, and cost effectiveness through engineering design improvements.
* Establish best practices supporting consistent, scalable manufacturing performance.

**Strategic Collaboration & Operational Excellence**

* Partner closely with R&D, Quality, Supply Chain, and Manufacturing leadership.
* Drive continuous improvement in engineering systems, processes, and infrastructure.
* Leverage manufacturing technologies, digital tools, and operational data to improve engineering outcomes.
* Support capital planning, resource allocation, and strategic investment decisions.
* Foster a culture of technical excellence, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.

**Qualifications**
------------------

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Biomedical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
* 15+ years of progressive engineering leadership experience.
* Demonstrated experience specifying, developing, and implementing automation across multiple manufacturing lines.
* Strong technical understanding of manufacturing processes, automation technologies, and engineering operations.
* Ability to balance strategic leadership with hands-on technical problem-solving.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* MBA or advanced degree.
* Proven success leading multidisciplinary engineering organizations through significant growth or transformation.
* Experience implementing advanced manufacturing technologies, including robotics and automated production systems.
* Strong understanding of Design for Excellence (DfX) and Design for Manufacturability (DFM).
* Knowledge of regulatory frameworks, quality systems, and compliance requirements.
* Experience leveraging Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), and digital manufacturing technologies.
* Demonstrated financial acumen, capital planning, project management, and resource allocation experience.
* Proven ability to attract, develop, and retain exceptional engineering talent.

**Work Environment**
--------------------

This position operates in both office and manufacturing floor environments and requires a leader who is comfortable engaging directly with engineering teams, manufacturing operations, and cross-functional stakeholders.

**Compensation & Benefits**
---------------------------

TransMedics is committed to equitable and transparent compensation.

The expected base salary range for this position is **$220,600 – $314,050 annually**, representing the company's current good-faith estimate of compensation.

Actual compensation will depend on factors including candidate experience, qualifications, skills, and specific work location.

This position may also be eligible for:

* Performance-based bonuses
* Equity compensation
* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* Retirement savings benefits
* Paid time off
* Wellness resources

TransMedics complies with all applicable U.S. pay transparency laws and does not request or consider salary history.

**About TransMedics**
---------------------

TransMedics is transforming organ transplantation through innovative technologies designed to improve the availability, utilization, and outcomes of donor organs.

Our mission is to help save more lives by advancing the science and technology of organ preservation and transplantation.

Join a growing organization where engineering innovation, technical excellence, and meaningful impact come together to advance life-saving technology.

This is a full-time, **on-site position** currently based at TransMedics' facility in Andover, MA.

TransMedics is preparing to transition operations to a new facility in **Somerville, MA**. Candidates should be aware of this upcoming move and must be willing and able to work on-site at both locations as the transition occurs.

Candidates must currently reside within commuting distance of the work location or be willing to relocate to the Greater Boston area.

This position requires regular collaboration with engineering, manufacturing, and cross-functional teams, including direct engagement on the manufacturing floor.

TransMedics is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and respectful workplace.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

TransMedics is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities throughout the application and hiring process.

We value the unique perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences of our employees and believe that an inclusive workforce strengthens our ability to innovate and fulfill our mission of saving lives.

**Employee Benefit:**

Medical with Health Reimbursement Account through Blue Cross/Blue Shield of MA

Dental

Vision

Healthcare Flexible Spending Account

Dependent Care Flexible Spending Account

Short Term Disability

Long Term Disability

401K Plan

Pet insurance

Employee Stock Purchase Plan

TransMedics is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, marital status, age, disability or protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

new_roles.title: Plant Manager
new_roles.description:
**JOB SUMMARY**

Reporting to the Region VPO, the Plant Manager has leadership responsibility for the facility and is the primary official in the Facility. The Plant Manager is key in planning, organizing, and executing the Facility’s day-to-day activities in a safe and proficient manner.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Facility leadership and general management activities.
* P&L responsibility for the Facility through creating and managing budgets that help achieve financial goals.
* Develop processes that will maximize stewardship, safety, quality, and productivity.
* The Plant Manager will ensure compliance with governing health/safety regulations and procedures.
* Assist in recruiting, hiring, retention, and developing of associates. This includes evaluations and performance documentation.
* Strategically create and adjust department activities, policies, and procedures to meet or exceed key performance metrics and customer satisfaction goals.
* Writes and adjust Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) to ensure standardization throughout network.
* Leads Facility teams on Gemba (waste) walks and manages solutions to improve findings
* Analyzes, identifies, and proposes action to the solution of problems with the operation of the division departments to increase the effectiveness of the operation.
* Ensures all DOT regulations are met in the transportation department
* Instrumental in the Development of key metrics and indices to drive improvement within daily, weekly, monthly, and annual results.
* Serves as a Facility spokesperson in cases of inquiry, feedback, or requests for special information to facilitate the accurate and precise flow of information.
* Aids in the solicitation of new or prospective business by participating in company meetings and any other market activities to foster the company’s recognition within the business community.
* Maintain high quality and safety standards by following specifications, local and federal governance, and Sysco’s quality programs (including 3rd party auditing).

**QUALIFICATIONS**

**Education**

* Bachelor’s Degree in Business, Engineering or Agriculture preferred or min 10 years’ experience in in operational leadership

**Experience**

* Minimum 10 years plant leadership in food production, manufacturing, costing, and distribution experience

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Financial responsibility
* Increasing leadership history
* Great verbal and written communication skills
* Lean Six Sigma or Lean Manufacturing experience

new_roles.description:
������ **MANUFACTURING LEADERS: What if your next role wasn't about inheriting someone else's operation—but building your own?**

**We are hiring for a Vice President & General Manager in Temple, Texas.**

This is a rare opportunity for an experienced manufacturing executive to take **40,000 square feet of open space** and turn it into a modern, high-performing manufacturing operation.

������ WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU?

You won't be stepping into a plant where everything has already been decided.

**You'll build it.**

������ Help design and launch a **40,000 sq. ft. manufacturing facility**

������ Recruit, develop, and lead a team of **50+ employees**

* ️ Influence equipment selection, automation, layout, workflow, and capital investment

������ Build the operating system, KPIs, accountability structure, and continuous-improvement culture

������ Own plant-level financial performance and operating results

������ Join an organization with strong customer demand, executive sponsorship, and significant growth ahead

Most importantly, you'll have the **authority to shape the facility, the team, and the way the operation runs**—not simply manage decisions someone else already made.

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

This opportunity is designed for a **builder**.

Someone who can walk the plant floor in the morning, work through production and capacity issues with the team, and sit down with the President later that day to discuss capital, performance, strategy, and growth.

You'll likely bring:

✔️ 15+ years of progressive manufacturing/operations leadership

✔️ Experience building, launching, relocating, or significantly expanding a manufacturing operation

✔️ Strong experience in **sheet metal fabrication, metal fabrication, welding, industrial equipment, HVAC/ductwork, process equipment, or engineered products**

✔️ Experience recruiting and building both salaried and hourly teams

✔️ A practical command of lean manufacturing, production planning, quality systems, constraint management, and continuous improvement

✔️ The ability to lead with **high standards, low ego, and genuine respect for people**

WHY THIS ROLE?

Because opportunities to truly **build something from the ground up** don't come along very often.

If you've spent your career thinking, “If I could build the operation myself, I'd do this differently…”

**This may be your opportunity to do exactly that.**

������ **Temple, Texas**

������ High-mix custom manufacturing

������ Significant long-term growth potential

������ Competitive executive compensation + performance-based incentive opportunity + comprehensive benefits

You should be proficient in:

* Leadership / People Management
* Industrial and Manufacturing Engineering
* Continuous Improvement
* Manufacturing Instruction (MI)
* Supervisory Experience
* Glass Fabrication
* Coaching and Mentoring Experience
* Operational Risk Management
* Workplace Safety & EHS Management
* Metal Casting Experience

new_roles.title: Plant Manager
new_roles.description:
We are seeking a skilled Plant Manager to oversee our co-manufacturing operations. The Plant Manager will be responsible for managing all aspects of plant operations while ensuring efficient production processes and maintaining high standards of quality and safety. This role requires strong leadership abilities, strategic thinking, and a deep understanding of manufacturing operations in a co-manufacturing setting.
 
 
**Responsibilities:** 

* Operational Leadership: Lead day-to-day plant operations, including production, packaging, maintenance, and quality control, to achieve production targets and quality standards.
* Team Management: Supervise and mentor a team of managers, supervisors, technicians, and support staff, fostering a culture of safety, quality, teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Production Planning: Develop and implement production schedules and resource allocation plans to optimize efficiency and meet customer demand while minimizing costs.
* Quality Assurance: Ensure adherence to quality assurance protocols and regulatory requirements, implementing corrective actions as needed to address non-conformities and improve processes.
* Safety and Compliance: Maintain a safe working environment by enforcing safety policies and procedures, conducting regular safety audits, and promoting a culture of safety awareness among employees.
* Budget and Cost Control: Manage plant budget and expenses effectively, identifying opportunities for cost savings and implementing measures to improve operational efficiency.
* Supplier and Customer Relations: Collaborate with suppliers and co-manufacturing partners to ensure timely delivery of materials and finished goods, and build strong relationships with customers to understand their needs and preferences.
* Continuous Improvement: Drive continuous improvement initiatives, such as Lean Manufacturing or Six Sigma methodologies, to streamline processes, reduce waste, and enhance overall plant performance.
* Reporting and Analysis: Prepare regular reports on plant performance, including production metrics, quality metrics, and financial KPIs, and provide analysis and recommendations for improvement to senior management.

**Qualifications:** 

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred.
* Proven experience (10+ years) in a managerial role within a co-manufacturing or food production environment.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, quality standards, and regulatory requirements.
* Excellent leadership and interpersonal skills, with the ability to motivate and develop a diverse team.
* Strategic thinker with a track record of driving operational excellence and achieving business objectives.
* Proficiency in ERP systems and Microsoft Office Suite; experience with manufacturing software (e.g., SAP, Oracle) is a plus.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with a focus on data-driven decision-making.
* Certification in Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other relevant certifications is desirable.
* #LI-JO1

Maker's Pride is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

new_roles.title: MRF Plant Manager
new_roles.description:
MRF Plant Manager

*Emterra Environmental USA | Lansing Material Recovery Facility*

**Location**

Lansing, Michigan

 

**Reports to**

Process Improvement Manager

 

**Employment type**

Full-time, salaried

 

**Compensation**

$90,000 - $100,000 plus 10% discretionary bonus

**About Emterra**
-----------------

Every day, Emterra Environmental USA helps communities recover resources, reduce waste and create a cleaner future. For 15 years we have partnered with Michigan communities, businesses and municipalities to deliver reliable waste and recycling services. What began as Emterra Group's first expansion into the U.S. has grown into a team of 215 employees serving 75 communities across the state.

**The Opportunity**
-------------------

We are looking for an experienced MRF Plant Manager to run day-to-day operations at our Lansing Material Recovery Facility. You will manage and coordinate production, logistics and maintenance, keep the plant compliant with all safety, environmental, labor and corporate requirements, and hold profit and loss (P&L) responsibility for setting and achieving the facility's budget and production targets. You will also play a key role in plant improvements and special projects.

**What You Will Do**
--------------------

* Supervise, coordinate and schedule plant staff and key operational personnel so the facility runs safely and efficiently.
* Optimize the processing of incoming recyclable material shift to shift, based on current intake volumes.
* Maximize daily production and uptime, increase productivity, minimize residue, audit inbound and outbound material, and produce commodities that meet buyer quality specifications.
* Own the plant's internal reporting, including daily bale counts, facility inspections, pre- and post-trip reports, daily MRF statistics and audit reports.
* Understand and monitor the flow of material through the system, and act proactively on suggestions and corrective actions to maximize throughput.
* Maintain maintenance calendars and logbooks for plant and mobile equipment.
* Have mechanical aptitude to ensure the daily trouble shooting and maintenance of the lines and to provide guidance to the maintenance team.
* Develop and manage the facility budget and production targets, and report on cost, throughput and commodity performance.
* Know and comply with all local, state and federal requirements for the facility and its operating permits and registrations, including MIOSHA and OSHA workplace safety standards and Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (EGLE) requirements.
* Protect the health and safety of every worker by making all workers aware of known hazards and ensuring they are trained on all applicable equipment, processes and duties.
* Lead plant improvement and special projects, and work closely with Collections, Sales, Maintenance, Safety and Finance teams.

**What You Bring**
------------------

* 5+ years of experience in a Material Recovery Facility (MRF), recycling, manufacturing or production environment, including 5 + years supervising a team production planning experience.
* Strong knowledge of maintaining the processing equipment (conveyors, screens, optical sorters, balers) and the mechanical processes with material flow.
* Working knowledge of MIOSHA/OSHA safety standards, including lockout/tagout, and of environmental compliance for a solid waste or recycling facility.
* Comfortable with data, reporting and Microsoft Office; experience with maintenance or production tracking software.
* A clear communicator and hands-on leader who can coach a team, hold people accountable and drive continuous improvement.
* Willingness to work flexible hours, including early mornings, or evenings or weekends as plant needs require.
* Post secondary diploma or degree in a related field in operations, engineering, or business management.

**Why Emterra**
---------------

* Stable, year-round work in an essential service.
* Competitive salary and benefits package: medical, dental, vision, 401(k).
* A supportive team that backs you on the plant floor and across the business.
* The chance to make a real difference in your community and the environment.
* Growth opportunities with a company that has been investing in Michigan for 15 years.

**How to Apply**
----------------

Apply online at emterrausa.com/pages/careers or send to hr.us @emterrausa.com. We thank all applicants for their interest; only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

*Emterra Environmental USA is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, height, weight, marital status or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law. Reasonable accommodations are available on request throughout the hiring process.*

new_roles.title: Senior Manager, Operations - Quality
new_roles.description:
**About the role:**
===================

This is a hands-on role with both strategic and executional scope. You will build and lead quality assurance and quality control standards across Operations, set the sampling, validation, and escalation practices the organization runs on, and partner closely with the Senior Manager, Operations - Payer Ops, the Human-in-the-Loop Operations leader, Product, and Engineering. You will report to the Head of Operations and help define the company's AI/Human QA strategy as Adonis scales.

**What you'll do:**
===================

**Own the Quality Program across Operations**
---------------------------------------------

* Define and own QA/QC standards, sampling methodologies, audit practices, and validation processes across AI agent outputs, human-executed work, and vendor-delivered operations.
* Develop & present quarterly plans and operating metrics; communicate progress and trade-offs; surface risks early + Work closely with the Head of Operations on strategic projects
* Lead quality assurance for payer workflows and agent outcomes, including new payer activations on the voice channel.
* Lead the development and implementation of a near-real-time QA Dashboard to provide visibility into quality, identify performance gaps, and track improvement over time.
* Partner with the operations team and external vendors to ensure work consistently meets Adonis's accuracy, operational, and compliance standards.
* Partner closely with the operations team to align on quality standards, remediation priorities, and operational performance.
* Collaborate with Product, Engineering, vendors, and cross-functional stakeholders to address quality gaps, improve workflows, and support strategic initiatives.
* Serve as the quality subject matter expert across Operations, ensuring quality considerations are incorporated into new workflows, product launches, and operational changes.

**Turn quality findings into operational and product improvements**
-------------------------------------------------------------------

* Translate and present quality trends and findings into actionable recommendations for Product, Engineering, and Operations, driving improvements from identification through implementation and validation.
* Leverage AI, automation, and internal tooling to increase the efficiency, accuracy, and scalability of QA/QC processes.
* Establish quality thresholds and escalation criteria for uncertain, complex, or high-impact outcomes.

**Build and lead a high-performing quality function**
-----------------------------------------------------

* Build and scale the Quality function, establishing clear goals, ownership, processes, and performance metrics.
* Lead, coach, and develop onshore and offshore team members, as the function grows.
* Develop and maintain SOPs, playbooks, training materials, and quality guidelines to support operational consistency and continuous improvement.

**Who you are:**
================

* 6+ years of experience
* Experience in healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM) is required, with practical understanding of payer, claims, or related revenue-cycle workflows.
* Experience building or leading quality assurance, quality control, or quality programs in a technology-enabled operations environment.
* Experience coaching a team and creating clarity across multiple workstreams.
* Experience defining operating standards, evaluating results, investigating failures, and ensuring corrective actions are effective.
* Strong cross-functional communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with Product, Engineering, customer-facing teams, and operational partners.
* Comfort moving between strategic planning and hands-on operational detail in a fast-changing environment.
* An AI-forward mindset and practical experience applying AI, automation, or intelligent tooling to improve quality and operational performance, with sound judgment about when human review is needed.

The base salary range for this position is $140,000 to $180,000. Base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. In addition to base salary, we also offer competitive equity and benefits packages.

**About Adonis**
================

Adonis is the leading AI orchestration platform for healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM), purpose-built for healthcare organizations seeking to transform their revenue operations. Traditional RCM processes often struggle with inefficiencies, costing providers up to 15% or more of their potential revenue. Through advanced automation, data science, and AI Agents, Adonis helps revenue teams detect vulnerabilities, optimize workflows, and deploy precise solutions that drive reliable and scalable financial outcomes.

Adonis is headquartered in New York City and has raised over $95M in funding, including a recent $40M Series C round led by Quadrille Capital with continued support from existing investors such as General Catalyst and Bling Capital. This funding supports our mission to restore sanity to RCM and equip provider groups and health systems with AI-driven revenue cycle operations at scale.

**Compensation Philosophy**
===========================

Actual base pay will depend on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Adonis determines compensation based on each candidate’s experience and qualifications relative to peers, and most new hires fall near the middle of the range. In addition to base salary, you’ll receive meaningful equity and great benefits.

**Perks at Adonis**
===================

* Competitive equity packages
* Employer-paid medical insurance
* Employer-paid dental insurance
* Employer-paid vision insurance
* Employer-funded HSA
* Parental leave
* Commuter benefits
* Office lunches every day
* Office snacks
* Generous PTO
* Located in 3 World Trade Center with easy access to all trains and the PATH, and amazing views of the city

Adonis is proud to be an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive culture that celebrates authenticity to win as one. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, protected veteran status, citizenship or immigration status, or any other legally protected characteristics.

At Adonis, we fully comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). We are dedicated to embracing challenges and creating an accessible, inclusive workplace for all individuals.

Compensation Range: $140K - $180K

new_roles.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering
new_roles.description:
**Relocation assistance is available for this position.**

**Who We Are**

Stored Energy Systems (SENS) is an award-winning manufacturer of premium quality power conversion products located in Longmont, CO. In business for over 50 years, SENS is the market leader with a proven track record of providing highly reliable battery chargers, DC power systems, and related products to industrial markets. For more information on our company please see our web site at www.sens-usa.com.

**View the SENS Product Catalog**

**Summary**

SENS is seeking a manufacturing engineering leader to help build and scale the organization, processes, and technical capabilities required for our next stage of growth. Supporting the expansion of existing manufacturing operations and establishing new operations at our Broomfield Systems manufacturing factory, this leader will establish the manufacturing engineering strategy, develop a multidisciplinary team, and translate business growth plans into manufacturing capacity and reliable production processes for our fastest-growing products.

This role leads manufacturing engineering, industrialization, tooling, test systems, automation, and technical production support for our systems products, with a strong emphasis on configure-to-order assembly manufacturing. Working closely with Production, Design Engineering, Quality, Safety, and Supply Chain, the Senior Manager will establish clear priorities, strengthen new product and production transfer readiness, and deliver measurable improvements in productivity, quality, cost, and equipment reliability.

A successful candidate will combine organizational leadership with practical technical judgment, building a team that can support daily production while executing the improvements and investments needed to scale.

**Responsibilities**

* Help to build and develop the manufacturing engineering organization. Assess current capabilities, define the team structure and staffing plan, recruit talent, and develop engineers and technical leaders to support SENS’s growth.
* Establish performance measures and execution discipline. Set departmental goals, review project and operational performance, communicate risks and resource needs, and hold the team accountable for measurable improvements in manufacturing readiness, capacity, productivity, and equipment reliability.
* Establish and execute the manufacturing engineering roadmap. Translate business growth, product plans, and production requirements into prioritized initiatives for manufacturing capacity, processes, tooling, test systems, automation, and equipment reliability.
* Lead manufacturing readiness for new products and production transfers. Partner with Design Engineering, Production, Quality, and Planning & Fulfillment to establish readiness criteria and ensure processes, equipment, tooling, test capability, documentation, and training are in place before production release.
* Develop scalable manufacturing processes and standards. Establish consistent methods for process development, validation, work instructions, engineering changes, and production controls across manufacturing locations while accommodating product-specific requirements.
* Expand manufacturing capacity and improve productivity. Lead engineering efforts in capacity analysis, line balancing, factory layout, workflow, cycle-time reduction, and constraint elimination to support production demand and improve labor efficiency.
* Provide reliable technical support to Production. Establish clear support coverage, escalation processes, and problem-solving practices that resolve production issues promptly and prevent recurrence while maintaining progress on strategic projects.
* Guide manufacturing technology development. Lead technical specialists responsible for manufacturing test systems, production software, tooling, and automation. Prioritize investments based on safety, quality, capacity, reliability, and financial return.
* Improve production equipment reliability. Establish equipment ownership, maintenance strategies, critical spare requirements, and preventive and predictive maintenance practices in partnership with Production and technical support teams.
* Manage projects, capital investments, and departmental resources. Develop business cases, budgets, schedules, and resource plans; oversee implementation and production acceptance; and verify that projects deliver their expected operational and financial benefits.
* Partner with Design Engineering on manufacturability. Incorporate manufacturing feedback early in product development and engineering changes to improve assembly, testability, quality, serviceability, and cost.
* Drive safe processes and sustained quality improvement. Partner with EHS and Quality to incorporate risk assessment, error prevention, root cause analysis, and corrective action into manufacturing processes and equipment changes.
* Oversee the development and maintenance of manufacturing processes, work instructions, test procedures, tooling, fixtures, automation systems, and production software solutions.
* Be directly accountable for engineering project delivery, manufacturing readiness, equipment reliability, and validated improvement benefits, while sharing accountability with Production and Quality for labor efficiency and first-pass yield (FPY).

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline, or an additional 4 tears of manufacturing engineering experience.
* Eight or more years of experience in manufacturing engineering, production engineering, industrialization, or a related technical manufacturing role.
* Three or more years of experience directly leading engineering or technical teams, including setting priorities, developing employees, allocating resources, and managing performance.
* Demonstrated success improving manufacturing performance, with measurable results in productivity, capacity, quality, cost, or equipment reliability.
* Experience developing and improving manufacturing processes, tooling, fixtures, work instructions, and production controls, including introducing new or revised products into production.
* Ability to lead engineers and technical specialists across manufacturing processes, test systems, automation, and production support, using sound technical judgment to evaluate solutions and resolve issues.
* Practical application of Lean Manufacturing and structured problem-solving methods, including root cause analysis and corrective action.
* Experience leading cross-functional projects with Production, Design Engineering, Quality, Safety, and Supply Chain, balancing daily production needs with longer-term improvement priorities.
* Experience planning and executing manufacturing improvement or capital equipment projects, including defining scope, schedules, resource requirements, and expected business results.
* Strong communication and organizational skills, with the ability to translate business objectives into clear team priorities and communicate progress, risks, and decisions.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in manufacturing of configure-to-order (CTO) and engineered-to-order (ETO) electrical systems such as switchgear, switchboard, etc.
* Experience with manufacturing software development, automated test systems, and data acquisition platforms.
* Experience using ERP systems such as SyteLine for BOM management, item masters, engineering changes, and manufacturing planning.
* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt, Black Belt, or equivalent certification.
* Experience managing departmental budgets and capital equipment projects from business case through production acceptance.

**Location:** Longmont, CO

**Base Compensation:** $120,000 - $175,000 is the projected annual base salary range for this role and will be determined on the candidate’s overall qualifications and experience.

**Bonus:** This position is eligible for an annual bonus based on individual and company performance.

**Closing Date:** December 15th. While we expect to keep the position open through this date, the posting may be extended or closed early based on applicant volume and hiring needs.

**Onsite Perks**

* Free gym with 24/7 access
* Free Electric Vehicle charging
* Breakfast and Lunch Café
* After hours Grab & Go snacks
* Basketball court
* Walking paths

**Benefits**

* Paid Time Off
* Paid holidays
* Medical insurance
* Dental insurance
* Vision insurance
* Short-term and long-term disability
* Life insurance
* 401(k) plan with immediate vesting
* Employee referral program
* Tuition reimbursement
* Professional development

At SENS, our culture is rooted in a set of core values that reflect who we are and how we work. In a recent 2025 poll, our employees identified the values that best define us: *“Innovative”, “Respectful”, “Inviting”, “Flexible”, “Collaborative”, and “Growth Driven”.* Our team describes us as a dynamic, forward-thinking company where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.

We pride ourselves on being an equal opportunity employer, fully dedicated to fostering inclusion and diversity. We welcome all applicants, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic.

We hope you're interested in making a difference with us. Even if you don't feel that you meet every qualification listed in this job description, we still encourage you to apply.

new_roles.title: Senior Manager, Industrial Engineering
new_roles.description:
**Continue to Grow with GXO.**

At GXO, we know our greatest asset is people like you - energetic, innovative people of all experience levels and talents who make GXO a great place to work. Your career matters to us because your passion and excitement will help keep our company moving forward.

 

As the **Senior Manager, Industrial Engineering**, you will lead the development of facility layouts and designs, labor standards, staffing and efficiency analyses, and identify cost-saving opportunities while supporting operational implementations.

**Pay, benefits and more.**

We are eager to attract the best, so we offer competitive compensation and a generous benefits package, including full health insurance (medical, dental and vision), 401(k), life insurance, disability and more.

**What you’ll do on a typical day:**

* Hire, train and develop industrial engineering staff; provide technical support and direction to site industrial engineers and managers
* Develop labor standards, process flow diagrams and job descriptions for new and existing operations
* Conduct time study analyses to estimate facility staffing requirements and establish production standards
* Identify, evaluate and implement productivity improvements
* Document processes to facilitate operational startups and provide on-site support as required
* Convert contract documents and SOWs into work instructions and operating procedures
* Analyze ongoing costs and compare them to prior cost and pricing estimates
* Select appropriate models for receiving, put-away, picking and packing solutions
* Identify storage and picking strategies based on product dimensions and activity levels
* Identify facility design requirements based on activity levels, product envelopes, product flow, transportation methods, building layout and power requirements
* Specify material handling and storage equipment solutions, including automation where justified
* Collaborate with IT resources to develop equipment requirements based on activity levels

**What you need to succeed at GXO:**

At a minimum, you’ll need:

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent related work or military experience
* 5+ years of experience working in a warehouse, distribution or 3PL environment
* Experience with Warehouse Management Systems (WMS)
* Experience with Labor Management Systems (LMS)
* Project management experience, including leading projects from concept through completion
* Experience with Lean Methodology and AutoCAD
* Familiarity with Six Sigma practices and principles

It’d be great if you also have:

* Advanced degree in Industrial Engineering or a related field
* 7 years of industrial engineering experience in a distribution environment
* 2 years of supervisory or management experience
* SQL experience

**We engineer faster, smarter, leaner supply chains.**

GXO is a leading provider of cutting-edge supply chain solutions to the most successful companies in the world. We help our customers manage their goods most efficiently using our technology and services. Our greatest strength is our global team – energetic, innovative people of all experience levels and talents who make GXO a great place to work.

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer including Disabled/Veterans.

GXO adheres to CDC, OSHA and state and local requirements regarding COVID safety. All employees and visitors are expected to comply with GXO policies which are in place to safeguard our employees and customers.

All applicants who receive a conditional offer of employment may be required to take and pass a pre-employment drug test.

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by people assigned to this classification. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and skills required of personnel so classified. All employees may be required to perform duties outside of their normal responsibilities from time to time, as needed. Review GXO's candidate privacy statement here.

new_roles.title: Senior Manager, Quality, Fauna
new_roles.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Fauna Robotics is building capable, safe, and delightful robots for everyday life. We are hiring a Senior Manager to lead the quality, test engineering, and reliability organization supporting our robots from development through production. 
In this role, you will improve product and manufacturing quality while building the testing capabilities needed to scale. Your organization will support new product introduction through volume production across our facilities, suppliers, and manufacturing partners. 
You will build the team and its engineering leadership, set the technical direction, and establish quality standards and validation processes. You will turn changing product and manufacturing needs into a roadmap that supports higher production volumes and additional sites. 
The ideal candidate is a technically strong engineering leader who has improved quality and reliability for products where hardware and software must work together. They can evaluate test strategies and guide critical supplier, production, and reliability investigations. They grow engineers and leaders, and make clear decisions on scope and priority while product designs and manufacturing processes are changing. 
 
Key job responsibilities 

* Architect the quality, test engineering, and reliability organization. Assess capability gaps, define the staffing and investment plan, and hire and develop the engineering leaders and teams needed to scale.
* Establish supplier and factory quality teams, with Fauna engineers embedded at manufacturing sites. Strengthen and scale the quality system to support new products and increasing production volumes.
* Define and lead the reliability strategy, working with our engineers to improve robot performance and durability.
* Build and scale reliability labs and test infrastructure to support product development and production growth.
* Scale and develop the manufacturing test engineering team, shaping its structure, growing its leaders, and strengthening its capabilities to support new products and increasing production volumes.
* Deploy and qualify production test systems across our facilities and manufacturing partners. Partner with the software and systems team on automation and traceable results, and improve repeatability, cycle time, and failure diagnosis.
* Partner with engineering and operations to embed quality, reliability, and testability into product design and production readiness.
* Establish quality and reliability metrics and use production, test, and field data to guide priorities and drive sustained improvement.

 
About the team 
Fauna Robotics, an Amazon company, is building capable, safe, and genuinely delightful robots for everyday life. Our goal is simple: make robots people actually want to live and interact with in everyday human spaces.
 
We believe that future won’t arrive until building for robotics becomes far more accessible. Today, too much effort is spent reinventing the fundamentals. We’re changing that by developing tightly integrated hardware and software systems that make it faster, safer, and more intuitive to create real-world robotic products.
 
Our work spans the full stack: mechanical design, control systems, dynamic modeling, and intelligent software. The focus is not just functionality, but experience. We’re building robots that feel responsive, expressive, and genuinely useful.
 
At Fauna, you’ll work at the frontier of this space, helping define how robots move, manipulate, and interact with people in natural environments. It’s an opportunity to solve hard problems across hardware and software with a team focused on making robotics accessible and joyful to build.
 
If you care about making robotics real for everyone and building systems that are as delightful as they are capable, we’re interested in hearing from you

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering or a related field
* 10+ years in quality, test engineering, or reliability for complex electromechanical products.
* 5+ years managing multidisciplinary engineering teams, with a track record of building organizations and developing engineers and leaders.
* Experience scaling supplier and manufacturing quality through NPI and production ramp, with strong knowledge of quality systems.
* Technical depth in reliability and manufacturing test engineering, with experience scaling test programs and infrastructure for integrated hardware-software products.
* Strong command of statistical analysis and structured problem-solving, with demonstrated success turning engineering data into product and process improvements.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* Experience with robotics or autonomous systems.
* Experience leading engineering managers or distributed teams across multiple manufacturing sites.
* Experience working with contract manufacturers and suppliers globally
* Experience with product safety certification or formal quality management standards.

 
Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. 
 
Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.

The base salary range for this position is listed below. Your Amazon package will include sign-on payments and restricted stock units (RSUs). Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. Amazon also offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance (medical, dental, vision, prescription, Basic Life & AD&D insurance and option for Supplemental life plans, EAP, Mental Health Support, Medical Advice Line, Flexible Spending Accounts, Adoption and Surrogacy Reimbursement coverage), 401(k) matching, paid time off, and parental leave. Learn more about our benefits at https://amazon.jobs/en/benefits.
