new_roles.title: Operations Director
new_roles.description:
Description:

Happy Corner Hospitality is the group behind Motek, Yalla Motek and Sesame Bakery. Since opening our first Motek in Downtown Miami in 2020, we've grown to 14 locations across South Florida and New York. Our Mediterranean menu draws on family roots in Lebanon, Morocco, Turkey, Yemen and beyond. We pride ourselves on delivering exceptional service and culinary experiences to our valued guests. As we continue to grow, we're seeking passionate, experienced individuals to join our group!

**Position Summary:**

As Operations Director, you will lead the overall performance of your assigned restaurants, guiding General Managers and their teams to deliver consistent, exceptional guest experiences across front and back of house. You will drive operational excellence, uphold brand standards and own the financial results of your locations, while developing strong leaders and a positive, high-performing culture. This role requires proven multi-unit leadership, sharp business judgment and a genuine passion for hospitality.

**Responsibilities include but are not limited to:**

*Operations & Guest Experience* 

* Oversee day-to-day operations across assigned locations, ensuring consistent front- and back-of-house performance
* Uphold brand standards and service at the highest quality across every location
* Conduct regular restaurant visits and operational audits, and follow up on action plans
* Ensure all corporate mandates, policies and daily reporting are completed and tracked
* Partner with the Culinary team to maintain food quality, consistency and kitchen standards
* Ensure all locations are clean, safe and well maintained, with equipment and repairs handled promptly
* Support new restaurant openings, including hiring, training and pre-opening readiness

*People & Leadership* 

* Lead, coach and develop General Managers and management teams
* Set clear goals and expectations, and hold leaders accountable for results
* Partner with HR on recruiting, hiring and staffing plans for management and key roles
* Identify and develop high-potential team members for growth into leadership roles
* Drive team morale, engagement, productivity and retention
* Enforce company standards, policies and expectations consistently across locations

*Financial Performance* 

* Own budgeted revenue, cost of sales (COS), labor, supplies and operating cash flow (OCF) for assigned locations
* Review monthly profit and loss statements with General Managers and drive action plans on variances
* Monitor operational expenses and identify opportunities to improve profitability
* Set and track sales forecasts and profitability goals
* Drive sales growth through marketing initiatives, community engagement and team incentives
* Keep C-suite leadership informed of performance, trends and key operational issues

**Benefits:**

* Competitive salary
* Wages paid weekly
* Growth opportunity
* 401(k) savings plan
* Paid time off
* Medical, dental and vision insurance
* Employee discounts

Requirements:

* 5+ years of leadership experience managing high-volume, fast-paced front-of-house restaurant operations
* Degree in hospitality or business preferred, or equivalent professional experience
* Strong knowledge of service standards, guest experience and regulatory compliance
* Experience managing budgets, labor, inventory and operating costs
* Ability to plan staffing, scheduling and team productivity
* Strong organization, multitasking and attention to detail
* Effective communicator with a collaborative, team-oriented leadership style
* Experience with marketing, sales initiatives and strategies to increase revenue is a plus
* Bilingual proficiency is a plus

new_roles.title: Sr Director or AVP, Fundraising Operations
new_roles.description:
**Sr Director or Assistant Vice President, Fundraising Operations**

Department: Lawrence Development

Reports to: Vice President, Development

FLSA Status: Exempt

The anticipated salary for this position starts at $124,100+ for the Sr. Director role and ranges up to $150,200+ for the Assistant Vice President role. The final pay will be determined based on several factors, including qualifications, experience, education, and years within the job or industry, with a strong emphasis on maintaining internal equity.

**Who we are and what we’re about:**

KU Endowment is an independent, nonprofit organization and the official fundraising foundation for the University of Kansas. We partner with donors in providing philanthropic support to build a greater KU.

As an employee of KU Endowment, you’ll witness firsthand the power of our donors’ generosity. You will join a talented and fun group of people who are inspired to help KU through the support of loyal alumni and friends. This support fuels excellence, enabling students and faculty to develop innovative programs and research that distinguish the university. We connect the philanthropic passions of donors with the needs of students, faculty and programs – and everyone benefits.

People are engaged. Purpose is ignited. Lives are changed.

**What we are looking for:**

The Senior Director/AVP, Fundraising Operations is the strategic operating leader responsible for translating advancement strategy into measurable fundraising performance. The role establishes the planning, analytics, management cadence, pipeline discipline, portfolio practices, and decision support that help fundraising leaders focus resources, improve execution, and achieve fundraising goals.

Serving as a trusted partner to executive leadership and frontline fundraising leaders, this role connects fundraising strategy, people, processes, data, and technology into a coherent revenue operating system. It provides visibility into performance, identifies risks and opportunities, and drives continuous improvement while enabling fundraisers and managers to spend more time building donor relationships and generating support.

The individual in this position is expected to embrace KU Endowment’s stated core values – collaboration, curiosity, empowerment, and excellence – and demonstrate support for them through professional interactions and activities.?

**What’s a typical day look like?**

* Build, lead, and evolve a high-performing fundraising operations function, including supervising, coaching, and developing development analysts, while establishing priorities, service standards, team capabilities, and scalable practices that support organizational growth and increasing complexity.
* Lead fundraising planning and operations strategy by translating institutional and campaign priorities into fundraising plans, goals, performance measures, resource allocation strategies, forecasting processes, and operational priorities.
* Direct fundraising forecasting, pipeline management, and feasibility assessment processes to improve revenue predictability, solicitation readiness, and achievement of fundraising objectives.
* Develop and implement portfolio management, prospect assignment, capacity planning, and fundraiser productivity frameworks that maximize donor coverage, fundraiser capacity, and fundraising performance.
* Provide executive leadership with analytics, forecasting, scenario modeling, and decision support that identify trends, risks, opportunities, and recommended actions.
* Design and facilitate management cadences, strategic reviews, and performance accountability processes that drive execution, continuous improvement, and goal attainment.
* Serve as the strategic business leader for fundraising operations technology, including CRM, reporting, analytics, and related platforms, ensuring systems, processes, and data support effective decision-making and fundraising outcomes.
* Lead organizational adoption of new Development focused processes, technologies, performance measures, and operating practices through effective change management, communication, training, and stakeholder engagement.
* Foster strong partnerships with fundraising leaders and cross-functional stakeholders to align strategy, data, technology, and operations in support of fundraising success.
* Regular and reliable attendance is essential for this position.
* Performs other duties as may be assigned.

**What’s required to be considered:**

* Bachelor’s degree required. Preference for a degree in business, finance, analytics, information systems, nonprofit management, higher education administration, or a related field.
* Master’s degree or equivalent advanced experience preferred.
* Management experience required. Experience leading cross-functional initiatives and managing or developing analytical/operations teams preferred.
* Typically 5–8+ years of progressively responsible experience in fundraising operations, advancement services, revenue operations, sales operations, analytics, business planning, or a related discipline.
* Experience in higher education, healthcare, nonprofit fundraising, or another complex relationship-driven organization preferred.
* Experience supporting campaign planning, enterprise fundraising goals, or large, distributed fundraising teams preferred.
* Experience with Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud or Salesforce fundraising implementations, data/BI platforms, and marketing or engagement technology preferred.

Senior Director, Fundraising Operations

A Senior Director demonstrates the ability and experience necessary to lead and optimize KU Endowment’s Fundraising Operations function, translating strategy into execution through planning, analytics, technology, forecasting, and team leadership.

* Typically 5+ years of progressively responsible experience in fundraising operations, advancement services, revenue operations, sales operations, analytics, business planning, strategy, or a related field.
* Demonstrated success leading an operations, analytics, advancement services, or revenue operations function and supervising professional staff.
* Experience developing and implementing forecasting, portfolio management, performance management, reporting, technology, or operational planning processes.
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and influence decision-making through analytics, insights, and operational recommendations.
* Capable of building, managing, and continuously improving a high-performing fundraising operations function.

Assistant Vice President, Fundraising Operations

An Assistant Vice President demonstrates the ability and experience necessary to lead KU Endowment’s Fundraising Operations function while serving as an enterprise-level strategic advisor, influencing fundraising strategy, organizational effectiveness, resource allocation, and transformational change initiatives across the organization.

* Typically 8+ years of progressively responsible experience in fundraising operations, advancement services, revenue operations, sales operations, analytics, business planning, strategy, or a related field.
* Demonstrated success leading complex operations, planning, analytics, advancement services, or revenue operations functions with organization-wide impact.
* Experience designing and implementing enterprise operating models, performance frameworks, resource allocation strategies, forecasting methodologies, or technology roadmaps across multiple teams or business units.
* Proven track record serving as a strategic advisor to executive leadership and leading significant organizational change and transformation initiatives.
* Demonstrated ability to influence organizational strategy and drive outcomes through leadership of cross-functional teams, stakeholders, and senior leaders, regardless of direct reporting relationships.

**What separates the best from the rest?**

* Exceptional strategic thinking, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate complex fundraising data, trends, and business needs into actionable recommendations and operational priorities.
* Demonstrated ability to develop performance frameworks, forecasting models, and management practices that improve fundraising effectiveness, accountability, and goal attainment.
* Deep understanding of fundraising operations, including campaign planning, pipeline management, portfolio strategy, prospect development, forecasting, performance management, and revenue planning.
* Ability to evaluate fundraising opportunities, project feasibility, philanthropic readiness, organizational capacity, and associated risks to support data-informed decision-making and resource investment.
* Strong data literacy and business intelligence skills, including the ability to leverage CRM platforms, reporting tools, analytics, and emerging technologies to inform strategy and improve organizational performance.
* Ability to lead technology-enabled change, drive adoption of new processes and systems, and continuously improve operational effectiveness across a complex organization.
* Exceptional written, verbal, presentation, and facilitation skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with executive leaders, managers, frontline fundraisers, and cross-functional partners.
* Demonstrated ability to influence without authority, build consensus among diverse stakeholders, and foster collaboration across teams and functions.
* Proven success leading, developing, and coaching high-performing teams while creating a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, innovation, and service excellence.
* Ability to establish and maintain professional and effective working relationships inside and outside KU Endowment.
* Ability to adapt to new procedures and technology.

**Physical Requirements:**

* A valid driver’s license.
* Must have access to reliable transportation to travel between multiple locations for training, donor meetings, networking, events and/or work-related activities.
* Must be able to respond quickly and effectively to directions and safety hazards.
* This job operates in a professional office environment. This role routinely uses standard office productivity machinery such as computers, keyboards and a mouse, laptops, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets and fax machines.
* This is largely a sedentary role; however, some filing is required. This would require the ability to move files, open filing cabinets and bend or stand as necessary.
* The ability to observe details at close range (within a few feet of the observer).
* The person in this position frequently communicates with donors, colleagues, students, and general public. Must be able to communicate with others effectively.
* Physical effort/lifting is limited – up to 40 pounds.
* Travel requirements are rare and can include the following, evenings, weekends, and out of town overnights as a regular part of the job.

new_roles.description:
Director of Operations

**Overview**
------------

Join Diversified Maintenance! We’re committed to delivering exceptional cleaning, landscaping, and restoration services for commercial facilities. Be part of a welcoming and collaborative team where innovation meets excellence. We offer steady, reliable work in janitorial management, full-time and part-time janitorial roles, maintenance, landscaping, and metal restoration. If you want to make a meaningful impact and build a lasting career, we have opportunities for you. Join us and grow with a leader in the industry!

**Job Description**
-------------------

Diversified Maintenance is hiring a Director of Operations. The Director of Operations oversees day-to-day operations of janitorial services for a specific business division. This senior level position is responsible for the development and implementation of a variety of strategies to maximize profits, while maintaining a high level of service quality within their division. Through continual evaluation and improvement, the Director of Operations positively impacts key performance indicators such as operational cost, service quality, and team development. This position provides oversight and leadership to team members and follows up on staff assignments.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Lead and manage the day to day operation through a team of top performers
* Manages the P&L for their operations
* Hold executive responsibility for all vertical operations, employee management, finances, and people related functions, sales growth, startups, account management, legal, and other operating elements of the business.
* Responsible for client relations and retention
* Manage and build performance teams, providing coaching, development and mentoring to a team of managers
* Develop and hold the team accountable to managing key performance indicators
* Stay current in business vertical and identify opportunities for company growth opportunities
* Provide timely feedback and guidance for team members on operational issues and concerns

**QUALIFICATIONS (MUST HAVE):**

* High school diploma or equivalent
* Minimum of five (5) years of management experience in janitorial industry
* Business level oral and written communication skills; ability to speak, read, and write fluently in English
* Ability to multitask and adapt to changing environments
* Excellent customer service skills; active listening skills
* Ability to lead and encourage teamwork; ability to negotiate and resolve conflict
* Ability to work in a team environment and demonstrate sound judgment
* Able to think independently
* Ability to analyze and deliver effective solutions
* Excellent organizational skills to include astute prioritization skills
* Proficient computer skills to include Microsoft and Google products

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS (NICE TO HAVE):**

* Bachelor’s degree or higher in business management
* Bilingual; ability to speak, read, and write in Spanish, French, or other languages
* Prior cleaning or janitorial experience
* Familiarity with custodial practices and commercial cleaning standards
* Knowledge of floor care techniques including buffing and waxing
* Experience in industrial cleaning or facilities maintenance

**BENEFITS:**

* Medical, dental, vision, basic life, AD&D, retirement plan and disability insurance
* Eight paid holidays annually, five sick days, and four personal days
* Vacation time offered at an accrual rate of 3.08 hours biweekly. Unused vacation is only paid out where required by law.

**Closing**
-----------

Diversified Maintenance is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race/ethnicity, age, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, genetic information, disability, protected veteran status or relationship/association with a protected veteran, or any other basis or characteristic protected by law.

If you have difficulty using the online system and require an alternate method to apply or require an accommodation, please contact our local Human Resources department.

new_roles.title: Regional Director of Operations
new_roles.description:
At El Pollo Loco, we are on a mission to be the nation’s leading fire-grilled chicken restaurant. When it comes to our people, we are all about growth. Whether that means specialized training, a clearly laid out career trajectory or collaborating cross-functionally, we are committed to the success of our people the same way we’ve been committed to the success of the El Pollo Loco brand for the last 50 years. In fact, we see you as our secret ingredient. While our chicken is fire, it’s our people who set us ablaze.
 
 
Our restaurants are only the tip of the flame! If you’re looking for an innovative, winning, and welcoming workplace, then a flamin’ good career in our Restaurant Support Center is right for you.
 
 
At our Support Center, we believe our best work is done Together, when departments collaborate and everyone is confident in contributing their ideas. This is why we are in the office 3 days per week.
 
 
Let’s Get Loco!
 
 
What’s in it for you!
 
 

* STRONG office culture recognized as a Great Place to Work® and driven by our core values: Simple. Together. Relentless. Ownership. Nimble. Growth
* Career growth opportunities
* Competitive pay and bonus potential
* Be an Owner: Equity Compensation
* Medical + Dental + Vision Insurance + HSA Savings Account
* 401(K) Retirement Plan with company match and immediate vesting
* Paid Vacation + Sick Pay + 12 Paid Holidays
* Employee Assistance Program
* Free El Pollo Loco food + restaurant discounts
* PerkSpot discounts program

**POSITION PURPOSE:** 
The Regional Director of Operations is responsible for driving El Pollo Loco’s success in the Los Angeles, CA region. They are responsible for providing operational expertise, strategic leadership and coaching. Directs, leads, manages and analyzes all aspects of the restaurant operations for the Areas under their direction to ensure achievement and maintenance of the regional sales, budgetary targets, controllable profit, performance metrics (e.g., service, quality, cleanliness, etc.), brand integrity, and compliance standards (e.g., food and restaurant safety, federal/state/local labor laws, etc.). Implements and executes strategic and tactical operational initiatives that support future business growth strategies. Oversees and manages adequate resource availability for existing and new restaurant openings including the attraction, retention, training, development and coaching of a high performing management team.
 
 
**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:** 

* Oversees all aspects of the region’s restaurant business, operations, and facilities. Directs and aligns company strategies with restaurant management activities.
* Utilizes reporting systems to determine trends in sales, cost of goods and guest services. Reviews, monitors and manages the financial progress of the individual restaurants and region, including food and labor costs, ensuring budgeted targets are achieved.
* Meets regularly with Area Leaders to coach, develop, train and review performance, share best practices and disseminate information on any areas where there is an opportunity for improvement (e.g., P&L, RCP, FSA, QSC, Mystery Shops, etc.). Develops action plans with Area Leaders to improve revenue, profitability and quality/service standards.
* Directs, manages and ensures the region’s successful and timely implementation of all marketing strategies and LTOs. Supports and inspects marketing strategies in building guest counts and sales.
* Provides effective and timely resolution to all guest and employee complaints, conflicts and employee relations that cannot be resolved at the Area Leader level.
* Ensures the region’s restaurants are in compliance with all local, regional, and national laws and have all the required documentation and paperwork.
* Leverages two-way communication with Field and Support Center employees. Represents the Operations perspective on prioritization, planning and promotions to inspire operational excellence, effective implementation and facilitate insights. Provides specific operational input and feedback into the development of new products and programs to ensure successful execution.
* Collaborates with Development, Human Resources, and Operations in the coordination and execution of new restaurant openings. Directs team selection, monitors the training and ensures the teams perform to El Pollo Loco’s standards. Participates in the local public relations support in all locations. Approves employee relocation within region ensuring moves are conducted in the most economical and efficient manner.
* Develops regional succession plans: evaluates open opportunities, assesses internal talent, oversees management training programs, and drives recruiting efforts to ensure adequate number of managers are available to sustain growth of the organization.
* Champions effective vertical and horizontal communications within the regional area including Company-wide news of interest, upcoming events, new facilities, promotions, product developments, “Best Practices” among peers, etc. Prepares thoroughly and delivers well-organized, dynamic and informative presentations to senior management as needed. Holds meetings with their respective teams on a regular basis to ensure fluid and consistent messaging.
* Creates and fosters a positive team environment through recognizing and reinforcing behaviors and results that are aligned with El Pollo Loco’s core values and culture. Ensures open channels for employee suggestions.
* Interacts professionally and ethically, constructively participating as a collaborative team leader in pursuit of common goals, including active attendance to meetings. Initiates cost-effective suggestions to improve operational procedures.
* Other activities, duties or responsibilities that are assigned by your supervisor.

QUALIFICATIONS – EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, LICENSE/CERTIFICATIONS:
 
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to satisfactorily perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodation will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job. The requirements listed below are representative of the education and/or experience required.
 
 
**Education/Work Experience:** 
High school diploma or equivalent (GED) required, BA/BS degree in Business Administration preferred. 8+ years QSR/multi-site restaurant experience as an Area Leader or District Manager required; 5+ years regional QSR management experience preferred; 3+ years El Pollo Loco experience preferred; and a track record of success in leading, managing, coaching and developing high performance teams.
 
 
**License/Certifications:** 
Current valid driver’s license required as frequent weekly travel is involved. Current ServSafe certification preferred.
 
 
**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:** 

* Experience with successfully recruiting, building, and developing a team (based on current and future needs).
* Confidence in execution of strategic initiatives.
* Must be decisive and able to make fact-based decisions.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving mindset and skills; meticulous attention to detail
* Ability to effectively communicate with internal and external business partners.
* Ability to prioritize and plan work assignments and work under pressure of frequent and tight deadlines.
* Ability to read, write, and interpret complex reports, documents, and correspondence.
* Adept at managing and prioritizing competing time sensitive requests while working well in a team atmosphere that may be under pressure.
* Ability to exercise independent judgment on matters of significance to the company.
* Ability to work weekends and extended work schedules as needed.
* Must be willing and able to travel locally within Southern California and to out-of-state restaurant locations, as needed by car or airplane.

Our Company
 
 
In 1980 the first American El Pollo Loco opened on Alvarado Street in Los Angeles, quickly becoming a destination for the best citrus-marinated, fire-grilled pollo in town. Over the past four decades, El Pollo Loco has grown into more than 500 restaurants across 9 states, becoming an L.A. mainstay and cultural benchmark along the way. And today, we continue to work just as hard to always provide customers with fresh and innovative L.A. Mex from our famous family dinners to Mexican entrees.
 
 
The pay range identified is the hourly or salary rate El Pollo Loco expects to pay for the posted position. This range does not include any benefits or bonus opportunities that might be available for the position based on position and eligibility criteria. Individual pay will vary based on a variety of factors including years of experience, industry experience, education, geography, etc.

new_roles.title: Vice President Quality Control
new_roles.description:
Position Overview:

Shape the future of quality and patient trust. Join us as the Vice President, Global Quality Control and lead a world-class laboratory network that powers our clinical and commercial programs across the globe. Reporting to the Chief Quality Officer, you will set the enterprise strategy and build a unified, high-performing Quality Control organization that delivers reliable data, inspection-ready laboratories, and timely product release support—while advancing standardization, digital innovation, scientific excellence, and operational performance.

Company Overview:

The work we do at FUJIFILM Biotechnologies has never been more important—and we are looking for talented candidates to join us. We are growing our locations, our capabilities, and our teams, and looking for passionate, mission-driven people like you who want to make a real difference in people’s lives.
 
 
Join FUJIFILM Biotechnologies and help make the next vaccine, cure, or gene therapy in partnership with some of the most innovative biopharma companies across the globe. We are proud to cultivate a culture that will fuel your passion, energy, and drive - what we call Genki. 
 
Fujifilm is globally headquartered in Tokyo with over 70,000 employees across four key business segments of healthcare, electronics, business innovation, and imaging. We are guided and united by our Group Purpose of “giving our world more smiles.” Visit: https://www.fujifilm.com/us/en/about/region/careers

Job Description:

Your impact In this enterprise role, your leadership will directly influence patient safety, product quality, inspection outcomes, batch disposition timelines, and continuity of supply across a diverse global portfolio. You will advise senior executives on investment, capacity, technology, organizational design, and regulatory strategy—shaping multi‑year business and quality plans. Your decisions will strengthen client trust, accelerate revenue recognition, reduce the cost of quality, and protect the company’s license to operate.

What you will do

* Define and execute a global Quality Control strategy, operating model, and multi‑year roadmap across sites, modalities, and development phases. Establish enterprise standards, clear decision rights, and governance forums that enable consistent, phase‑appropriate control while allowing justified site or platform differences.
* Provide executive oversight of end‑to‑end Quality Control operations, including analytical, biochemical, biological, microbiological, raw‑material, in‑process, release, and stability testing; as well as environmental and utility monitoring. Ensure capacity, prioritization, and flawless execution to meet program milestones, product disposition, client commitments, and uninterrupted supply.
* Govern the analytical method lifecycle from early development through transfer, qualification, validation, comparability, continued performance verification, and retirement. Ensure control strategies and specifications evolve appropriately through clinical development, process performance qualification, launch, and sustained commercial supply.
* Set global expectations for current good manufacturing practice, applicable good laboratory practice principles, data governance, principles that ensure data are attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original, accurate and complete, laboratory investigations, out of specification and out of trend management, corrective and preventive action effectiveness, change control, and audit readiness. Lead enterprise strategy and executive response for regulatory inspections and critical client audits.
* Build and deliver the digital and technology roadmap for laboratory information management systems, electronic laboratory notebooks, laboratory execution systems, chromatography data systems, laboratory automation, advanced analytics, and instrument connectivity. Sponsor validated deployment, master‑data governance, cybersecurity, and adoption that improve right‑first‑time outcomes and cycle time.
* Direct enterprise Quality Control capacity planning, capital prioritization, make‑versus‑buy decisions, laboratory footprint strategy, and governance of external testing partners. Align resources and contingency plans with demand forecasts, technology transfers, new product introductions, and network resiliency needs.
* Establish enterprise metrics and management review for on‑time testing and release support, lead time, invalid results, out of specification and out of trend rates, investigation cycle time, corrective and preventive action effectiveness, stability execution, method performance, cost, and productivity. Drive risk‑based priorities, Lean practices, and cross‑site learning to deliver sustainable improvement.
* Serve as the senior Quality Control liaison for strategic clients, regulatory authorities, and executive governance. Translate complex laboratory, method, and compliance risks into clear business implications, negotiate technically sound solutions, and ensure commitments are realistic, documented, and delivered.
* Build and lead a global organization through senior leaders. Define capabilities and succession plans, develop technical career paths and communities of practice, and cultivate a culture of scientific rigor, transparency, accountability, inclusion, and proactive risk management.
* Own escalation and coordinated response for significant Quality Control events, laboratory constraints, critical data‑integrity concerns, assay failures, method or specification issues, and testing disruptions. Make or recommend risk‑based decisions on testing strategy, product impact, remediation, and continuity of supply.
* Perform other duties in support of the broader Global Quality strategy and company objectives.

Minimum qualifications

* Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biology, Microbiology, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Engineering, or a related scientific discipline, with fifteen or more years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or contract development and manufacturing organization Quality Control; or a Master’s degree with ten or more years.
* Ten or more years of people leadership, including five or more years leading senior leaders with accountability for multiple laboratories, sites, or functional areas.
* Demonstrated leadership of Quality Control across development and commercial stages, including method transfer, qualification and validation, release and stability testing, microbiology, and environmental and utility monitoring.
* Proven experience with global regulatory inspections and client audits, and with complex out of specification, out of trend, data‑integrity, and laboratory‑compliance matters.
* Experience managing budgets, capital portfolios, headcount, capacity, external laboratories, and enterprise transformation in a matrixed global organization.
* Executive‑level communication and client‑facing experience in a regulated, technically complex environment.

Preferred qualifications

* Advanced scientific degree and/or a Master of Business Administration.

identity_held_roles.title: Sr. Manager, Optimus Operations
identity_held_roles.description:
**What To Expect**
The Senior Manager, Optimus Operations sets the vision and strategic path for Production, Maintenance, and Engineering within a major shop at Tesla’s new Optimus Factory in Austin, Texas. Openings span operations leadership across multiple shops—including Plastics, Machining, Actuators, and Assembly. Each role leads their shop teams and cross-functional partners to achieve Safety, People, Quality, Production/Delivery, and Cost KPI targets.
 
 
This role is responsible for production and resource planning; coaching, mentoring, and developing leaders; launching new Optimus manufacturing processes and programs successfully; and daily tactical planning and execution to achieve the build plan and meet safety, quality, rate, and cost targets. The person in this role must guide the team through complex issues, distill large volumes of data to solve problems, and drive day-over-day continuous improvement in a high-volume, high-precision factory environment.
 
 
This Senior Manager provides hands-on support, leadership, and direction on all operational, team morale, and equipment-related matters. The person in this role builds teams that work cohesively and perform at the highest level—keeping Tesla’s mission and the goals of the Optimus program in mind—while partnering closely with peer shop leaders and factory leadership across the Austin Optimus Factory.
 
 
**What You'll Do**- Set the vision and strategic path for Production and Maintenance in an assigned Optimus shop and lead the team to Safety, People, Quality, Production, and Cost KPI targets
- Drive tactical planning to hit the production build plan with the highest safety, quality, and yield, including identifying bottlenecks and addressing availability, efficiency, and yield constraints
- Launch new Optimus programs and lead production ramps and product/process design changes through resource planning, program management, and partnership with NPI, Manufacturing Engineering, Design Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain
- Guide the team through root cause analysis, first-principles thinking, and data-driven problem solving while maintaining standardized work and quality/safety compliance
- Coach, mentor, and develop Production, Maintenance, and Engineering leaders, instill process standardization and training, and drive continuous improvement
- Lead the maintenance organization on equipment availability, preventive and predictive maintenance, spare parts strategy, and uptime improvements for shop-critical assets
- Build a high-performing team with clear goals and feedback, improve morale with HR, and collaborate with peer shop Senior Managers to share best practices
**What You'll Bring**- Degree in Manufacturing, Mechanical, Chemical, Electrical, Materials, or Industrial Engineering preferred, or equivalent experience
- 7–10 years of leadership and manufacturing experience, preferably in automotive, robotics, plastics, precision machining, electromechanical assembly/actuators, general assembly, or another highly technical manufacturing environment
- Analytical, detail-oriented, self-driven critical thinker who communicates proactively and works well in a fast-paced, multicultural factory environment
- Experience with process-improvement methodologies, DOE/statistical methods, lean and world-class manufacturing practices, and standing up or ramping new factories, shops, or production lines
- Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to work under pressure, juggle competing priorities, and meet tight deadlines
- Ability to use structured problem-solving methods such as 8D, fishbone diagrams, and 5-Why analysis to resolve production problems
- High-level leadership and decision-making skills with a strong sense of urgency in a greenfield/new-factory ramp, plus proficiency in MS Office, Visio, CAD, SPC, data-analysis tools, Jira, Tableau/BI dashboards, and project-management tools
**Benefits**
Along with competitive pay, as a full-time Tesla employee, you are eligible for the following benefits at day 1 of hire:
 
- Medical plans > plan options with $0 payroll deduction
- Family-building, fertility, adoption and surrogacy benefits
- Dental (including orthodontic coverage) and vision plans, both have options with a $0 paycheck contribution
- Company Paid (Health Savings Accounts) HSA Contribution when enrolled in the High-Deductible medical plan with HSA
- Healthcare and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
- 401(k) with employer match, Employee Stock Purchase Plans, and other financial benefits
- Company paid Basic Life, AD&D
- Short-term and long-term disability insurance (90 day waiting period)
- Employee Assistance Program
- Sick and Vacation time (Flex time for salary positions, Accrued hours for Hourly positions), and Paid Holidays
- Back-up childcare and parenting support resources
- Voluntary benefits to include: critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, theft & legal services, and pet insurance
- Weight Loss and Tobacco Cessation Programs
- Tesla Babies program
- Commuter benefits
- Employee discounts and perks program
- Earned Wage Access: Real-time pay access paid daily, subject to eligibility and schedule (applicable for below Sr. Managers levels)

identity_held_roles.title: Director of Continuous Improvement
identity_held_roles.description:
**Director of Continuous Improvement**

* **Director of Continuous Improvement**
* **Greater Charlotte Area**
* **$170,000 to $200,000 + Bonus + Strong Company Benefits**

A leading global industrial manufacturer is seeking a Director of Continuous Improvement to drive operational excellence, Lean transformation, and productivity improvements across multiple manufacturing facilities. Reporting directly to the C-suite, this high-impact leadership role will be responsible for deploying enterprise-wide continuous improvement strategies, developing Lean capabilities, and delivering measurable gains in safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost performance. If you're passionate about building high-performing operations, coaching teams, and leading large-scale Lean transformations, this is an outstanding opportunity to make a lasting impact within a growing international organization.

**Key Responsibilities**
:

* Lead the deployment of Lean Manufacturing and Continuous Improvement strategies across multiple manufacturing sites.
 
 Champion the use of Lean methodologies including Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping, Standard Work, SMED, TPM, and Six Sigma tools.
* Support plant leadership teams in identifying and executing operational improvement opportunities.
* Coach and mentor Plant Managers, Operations Leaders, CI Managers, and Production Leaders.
* Develop Lean competencies throughout the organization through training, workshops, and hands-on coaching.
* Support facility footprint optimization, cost reduction programs, and operational strategy deployment.
* Pioneer the implementation of digital manufacturing and Smart Factory technologies.
* Ensure operational excellence principles are embedded into daily management systems and site culture.

**The successful candidate will ideally have**
:

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related discipline,
* 10+ years of experience leading Lean Manufacturing and Continuous Improvement initiatives within a manufacturing environment.
* 8+ years of experience applying Lean methodologies in high-volume industrial or automotive manufacturing operations.
* Proven experience driving measurable improvements in productivity, quality, and cost reduction.
* Certified Six Sigma Black Belt (CSSBB).
* Multi-Site Manufacturing experience

**Desired Skills and Experience**
\* Bachelor's degree in Business, Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related discipline,
 
\* 10+ years of experience leading Lean Manufacturing and Continuous Improvement initiatives within a manufacturing environment.
 
\* 8+ years of experience applying Lean methodologies in high-volume industrial or automotive manufacturing operations.
 
\* Proven experience driving measurable improvements in productivity, quality, and cost reduction.
 
\* Certified Six Sigma Black Belt (CSSBB).
 
\* Multi-Site Manufacturing experience

identity_held_roles.description:
**Job Description:**

**Who We Are:**

At Cart.com, we're **defining the future of commerce.**

Founded to solve the growing complexity of modern commerce, Cart.com helps businesses simplify how they sell, fulfill, and deliver products to their customers. We bring together technology, services, and logistics infrastructure into one connected platform, making it easier for organizations to grow, operate efficiently, and navigate an increasingly fragmented commerce landscape.

We work with brands, retailers, manufacturers, and public sector organizations to support every stage of the customer journey, from ecommerce and order management to fulfillment, distribution, and delivery. By combining software, expertise, and a nationwide logistics network into a unified solution, we help our customers move faster, operate smarter, and scale with confidence.

But what truly sets Cart.com apart is our people. We're builders, problem-solvers, and innovators who thrive on turning big challenges into meaningful outcomes for our customers. Every day, we're helping shape the future of commerce while creating opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact.

If you're energized by solving complex problems, collaborating with talented teammates, and helping build what's next, we'd love to hear from you.

**Cart.com Milestones**

* Founded in 2020 with a vision to build the first truly unified commerce platform.
* Achieved unicorn status with a valuation exceeding $1 billion.
* Raised more than $475 million to support continued growth and innovation
* Expanded a nationwide commerce and logistics network that helps organizations scale, fulfill, and grow across channels.
* Recognized by Inc.'s Power Partner Awards for helping businesses grow and scale.
* Recognized as an award-winning employer for four consecutive years, reflecting our commitment to building an environment where talented people can grow, innovate, and make an impact.

**Our values:** Cart.com is building a company that is committed to living out these 6 core values:

* **Be brand obsessed:** Our lives are shaped by the brands we interact with daily. We obsess over the brands we serve, and about the things they care about.
* **Think beyond the box:** “We’ve always done it that way” is not a phrase uttered often at our office. We create creative solutions to complex problems.

* **Don’t give up:** We learn from our challenges and see them for what they are; great building blocks to an amazing brand story.
* **Speak up:** We communicate clearly and directly because we care deeply. Communication is the bedrock of our community.
* **Work together:** We’ve built a team that prides itself on diversity of thought and background. Collaboration is better with contrast.
* **Remember to be human:** We work hard, but we leave room for the people, places and things that we love

**AI is part of how we work. It's not doing the hiring.** 
 
We'll use AI in parts of our process and we think you should feel free to use it too — for research, prep, whatever helps. But our interviews exist to meet *you*, not your best AI-assisted draft. Real people make every call here. Any questions about how this works, just ask.

**Remote:**

This position is fully remote and open to candidates in AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, DE, FL, GA, HI, IL, IN, KY, LA, MA, MD, MI, MO, MS, NC, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA, WA. The salary range for this role is $175,000-200,000 annually. Actual compensation may vary based on geographic location, experience and qualifications. This role is eligible for bonus, equity and benefits including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), paid time off. Applications accepted through 1-31-2027. We comply with all applicable pay transparency laws in the states where we operate.

**The Role:**

The Director, Quality and Compliance leads the quality function for Cart.com’s federal pharmaceutical distribution business across four sites. This leader will standardize and strengthen an established quality program, develop site quality leaders, ensure consistent application of procedures, and serve as the primary quality point of contact for client reporting, audits and product-quality events.

This is approximately a 70% strategic leadership and 30% hands-on role. The Director will not build the program from the ground up, but will assess the current-state program, make targeted improvements, and ensure teams consistently execute against client, regulatory and network requirements. The role is remote with approximately 30% travel.

The role offers the opportunity to influence the quality standard for a growing federal business and help prepare the organization to support additional federal programs over time.

**What You’ll Do**

* Lead and develop site quality leaders across Maryland, Goodyear, Temecula and Memphis, establishing clear accountability, delegation and follow-through.
* Standardize quality procedures and expectations across the network while refining the existing quality management system and closing identified gaps.
* Ensure sites remain prepared for client and regulatory audits; support audit planning, host or coordinate inspections, and oversee timely responses and corrective actions.
* Serve as the primary quality point of contact for pharmaceutical product excursions and related client reporting, ensuring submissions are accurate, complete and timely.
* Oversee quality processes supporting receiving, quarantine, release, disposition, returns, destruction, recalls, deviations, corrective and preventive actions, change control, training, complaints and document control.
* Guide quality decisions for controlled-temperature pharmaceutical products, including refrigerated, frozen and ultra-cold storage and distribution.
* Partner with site Operations leaders and Cart.com’s Compliance team to implement operational changes required to meet quality standards and client expectations.
* Use quality metrics, audit findings, client feedback and site observations to identify risk, prioritize improvements and report progress to senior leadership.
* Travel to sites for audit preparation, team development, quality reviews and issue resolution.

**Who You Are:**

 

* You are a strategic, hands-on quality leader who can set direction while stepping into audits, excursions and site-readiness work when needed.
* You lead through others, delegate clearly, establish checkpoints and hold site quality leaders accountable for follow-through.
* You put the client’s requirements first, ask the right questions and respond with accurate, timely information.
* You communicate with credibility and composure across clients, regulators, Operations, Compliance and senior leadership.
* You are highly organized and disciplined, ensuring commitments, documentation and escalations do not get lost.
* You build strong cross-functional partnerships and can influence operational changes without creating a separate quality silo.
* You adapt to changing federal-client requirements while maintaining consistent quality standards and sound judgment.
* You develop people, address performance gaps directly and create a culture of ownership across a distributed team.

**What You’ve Done:**

 

* 7+ years of progressive pharmaceutical quality experience, including work in a current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) facility and meaningful pharmaceutical distribution, logistics or 3PL quality exposure.
* 5+ years of people-leadership experience with demonstrated success delegating, developing leaders and holding teams accountable.
* Worked in pharmaceutical distribution, wholesale, logistics or third-party logistics (3PL). Manufacturing experience alone is not sufficient without meaningful distribution-quality exposure.
* Applied cGMP, Good Distribution Practice (GDP), controlled-document and standard operating procedure requirements in a regulated pharmaceutical environment.
* Prepared for or led audits involving the U.S. Food and Drug Administration or comparable regulators, including managing responses and follow-up actions.
* Supported pharmaceutical product release, disposition, holds, recalls or temperature-excursion decisions in a regulated distribution setting.
* Written, revised or implemented quality procedures and documentation, then ensured consistent execution across teams or sites.
* Led a distributed or multi-site team and built accountability through site leaders rather than personally owning every task.
* Managed a significant client, product-quality or regulatory issue requiring coordination across Quality, Operations and Compliance.
* Earned a bachelor’s degree in life sciences, pharmacy, biology, chemistry or a related field, or bring an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
* Ability to travel up to 30%.

**Nice to Haves:**

 

* Background supporting federal health programs or agencies such as HHS, DLA, ASPR, BARDA, DoD or VA.
* Experience with pharmaceutical 3PLs, wholesalers, state licensing or NABP accreditation.
* Hands-on experience with vaccines or other cold-chain and ultra-cold pharmaceutical products.
* Knowledge of Drug Supply Chain Security Act requirements and suspect or illegitimate product processes.
* Relevant certifications such as ASQ Certified Quality Auditor, Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence, Certified Pharmaceutical GMP Professional or Lead Auditor.
* Master’s degree in a life-sciences or related discipline.
Direct leadership of quality teams 

 
 

**Physical Demands & Working Conditions:**

 

* Remote work environment with regular computer and video-conference use.
* Ability to travel by air or ground up to 30% and work onsite in warehouse, pharmaceutical distribution and temperature-controlled environments.
* Ability to move through operating areas and wear required personal protective equipment when visiting sites.
* Flexibility to support audits, client needs or quality events outside standard business hours when required.

Eligibility Requirement: This position is open only to U.S. citizens due to applicable federal requirements. By applying, you confirm that you are a U.S. citizen and can provide acceptable documentation verifying your status if selected. 
 
If you are not a U.S. citizen, please do not apply for this role.

Cart.com is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

identity_held_roles.description:
***POSITION PURPOSE:***

The Director of Quality Improvement operates under the leadership and direction of the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) and Chief Operating Officer (COO). The CMO maintains direct clinical oversight of clinical quality improvement activities and regulatory quality programs. The Director of Quality Improvement provides organization-wide leadership for EVCHC's quality improvement program. The Director establishes the quality strategy in partnership with executive, clinical, operational and compliance leaders; converts organizational goals and regulatory requirements into measurable work plans; and leads improvement efforts that strengthen patient outcomes, safety, access, equity and care experience. The Director is accountable for reliable quality data, required clinical quality reporting, continuous improvement methods, Patient Centered Medical Home recognition, and the performance of the Quality Improvement Department.

 

***MAJOR POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES AND FUNCTIONS:***

**Quality Strategy and Governance**

* Lead the development, implementation and annual evaluation of EVCHC's organization-wide Quality Improvement and Quality Assurance Plan in alignment with the strategic plan, clinical standards and applicable Health Center Program requirements.

* Establish annual quality priorities, measures, targets, owners and timelines with executive and clinical leadership. Monitor progress and recommend corrective action when performance does not meet established goals.

* Lead or support the Quality Improvement Committee and related workgroups. Prepare agendas, dashboards, meeting materials, decisions and follow-up reports for executive leadership and the Board of Directors, as requested.

* Advise executive leaders on emerging quality risks, performance trends, resource needs and opportunities to improve care delivery across sites and service lines.

* Promote a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, patient safety and learning throughout the organization.

**Department Leadership**

* Direct the work of the Quality Improvement Department, including recruitment, onboarding, supervision, coaching, performance evaluation, workload assignment and staff development.

* Develop departmental goals, staffing plans, procedures and budgets that support timely completion of quality priorities and reporting obligations.

* Set clear expectations for the accuracy, timeliness and usability of analyses, audits, reports and improvement support provided by the department.

* Build effective working relationships with clinical care teams, Operations, Information Technology, Compliance, Human Resources, Finance, Behavioral Health, Dental and other departments involved in quality outcomes.

**Quality Measurement and Reporting**

* Oversee the collection, validation, analysis and submission of clinical quality measures and required reports, including Uniform Data System measures, population health platforms transition and readiness, HEDIS and payer measures, grant measures and internal quality indicators.

* Develop and maintain executive, provider, site and service-line dashboards that show current performance, trends, disparities, targets and improvement actions.

* Track provider and care-team performance, identify variation and care gaps, and provide leaders with actionable information while maintaining appropriate confidentiality and data-use standards.

* Establish data-validation controls and documentation so that quality reports can be reconciled to source systems and used as an organization-wide source of truth. Partnering with Director of Data and IT operations for oversight on data governance committee.

* Present quality findings in clear written and verbal reports to the Board, executive leadership, managers, providers, staff, health plans and external reviewers, as appropriate.

**Performance Improvement**

* Lead Plan Do Study Act cycles, root-cause analyses and other structured improvement methods from problem definition through implementation, evaluation and sustainment.

* Partner with clinical and operational leaders to improve preventive care, chronic disease outcomes, access, continuity, patient experience, care coordination, documentation and other priority measures.

* Translate data findings into practical workflow changes, training, decision support, audit tools and accountability processes that can be sustained across sites.

* Evaluate improvement results, identify lessons learned and spread effective practices to other care teams, programs or locations when appropriate **Regulatory Readiness and Patient Safety**

* Lead the quality components of Patient Centered Medical Home recognition and renewal, including evidence collection, workflow assessment, documentation, staff education and sustainment of recognized practices alongside Director of compliance.

* Partner with Compliance Director, Risk Management, clinical leadership and Operations on quality-related readiness for HRSA operational site visits, FTCA deeming and risk-management activities, health plan audits, accreditation reviews and other external assessments.

* Support corrective action plans with the Director of Compliance arising from audits, quality reviews, safety events or regulatory findings. Define measures, monitor completion and verify that corrective actions are effective and sustained.

* Analyze trends in patient safety events, grievances and quality-of-care concerns with the appropriate leaders while protecting confidentiality and following reporting requirements.

* Maintain organized records of quality plans, committee actions, reports, audits, improvement projects and supporting evidence required for oversight and external review.

**Clinical Analytics and Health Information Technology**

* Direct the clinical analytics program and define reporting requirements that support clinical decision-making, population health management and performance improvement.

* Partner with Information Technology and system vendors to improve data extraction, interfaces, registries, care guidelines, clinical decision support, templates and reporting tools used for quality measurement.

* Lead data-governance practices for quality information, including measure definitions, ownership, validation, access, change control and resolution of reporting discrepancies.

* Assess the quality and workflow impact of new digital tools and automation used in clinical or quality processes and recommend safeguards, testing and performance monitoring before broad implementation.

* Recommend redesign of workflows affected by the electronic health record, patient portal, population health platforms and other clinical information systems.

**Organizational Responsibilities**

* Participate in executive, management, clinical and staff meetings related to quality priorities and organizational performance.

* Maintain current knowledge of FQHC quality requirements, clinical quality measures, health plan expectations and recognized improvement practices.

* Protect patient, employee and organizational information and comply with HIPAA, confidentiality, cybersecurity and records-management requirements.

* Perform other job-related duties as assigned within the scope of the position.

***POSITION REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS:***

**Education and Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in public health, health care administration, nursing, health sciences, informatics or a related field is required. A master's degree is preferred.

* At least five years of progressive experience in health care quality improvement, population health, clinical analytics or health care program management is required, including at least three years of supervisory or department leadership experience.

* Experience in a Federally Qualified Health Center, community health center or other safety-net setting is strongly preferred.

* Experience leading cross-functional improvement projects and preparing quality reports for executives, governing boards, health plans or regulatory agencies is required.

* Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality, Lean or Six Sigma certification, or comparable quality-improvement training is preferred.

**Knowledge and Skills**

* Working knowledge of continuous quality improvement methods, patient safety practices, clinical quality measurement, health equity and population health management.

* Knowledge of HRSA Health Center Program expectations, Uniform Data System reporting, HEDIS measures, Patient Centered Medical Home standards and payer quality programs is strongly preferred.

* Advanced ability to collect, validate, analyze and present health care data and to translate findings into operational decisions and improvement plans.

* Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint and experience using electronic health records, population health platforms, data visualization tools or clinical reporting applications. Experience with NextGen or comparable systems is preferred.

* Strong leadership, project management, facilitation, written communication and presentation skills, with the ability to build accountability across departments .

* Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet reporting deadlines, exercise sound judgment and communicate sensitive performance information professionally.

* Demonstrated commitment to serving medically underserved communities and reducing disparities in access, care and health outcomes.

***WORKING CONDITIONS/PHYSICAL/MENTAL ABILITIES AND PROCESSES:***

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

 

* Work is performed primarily in an office and health center environment and requires regular travel among EVCHC sites and occasional travel to meetings or trainings.

* The position requires extended periods of sitting and computer use, as well as standing, walking, bending, reaching, speaking, hearing and seeing sufficient to perform assigned duties.

* The employee must be able to communicate clearly, review detailed reports, maintain concentration, manage competing deadlines and work effectively in shared office and clinical environments.

* The employee must be able to lift and carry materials and equipment weighing up to 20 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation.

identity_held_roles.description:
**Position Overview:**

As the Regional Senior Manager of Post Production/IQR, you will have the unique opportunity to partner closely with several different teams at multiple sites (including IC leadership, reconditioning, and support teams) to drive the strategy behind the development and deployment of Post Production & Quality programs, as well as manage continued performance of internal and external vendors. We are looking for a resourceful self-starter who will set the tone for the successful and fast-paced growth of our Inspection Centers. The Regional Senior Manager of Post Production/IQR role will be heavily focused on leading our teams to effectively close operational gaps and establishing standardized practices that will drive exceptional quality.

**What you'll be doing:**

* Driving successful execution amongst our Post Production teams by effectively leading and developing team members and creating and implementing new processes and systems.
* Identifying issues or roadblocks to execution and quickly taking action to problem solve and implement effective solutions across a large and quickly evolving platform.
* Providing clear direction and necessary support to ensure operational gaps are being closed in a timely manner.
* Working with key business partners to develop systems, metrics, reporting, and staffing models for our Post Production processes and teams.
* Effectively leading and developing onsite personnel at third-party production locations.
* Managing quality of internal and external vendors responsible for producing units for Carvana.
* Establishing effective working relationships with internal and external partners.
* Creating and successfully executing large-scale change management initiatives and new process rollouts.
* Other duties as assigned.

**What the job requires:**

To be able to do your job at Carvana, there are some basic requirements we want to share with you.

* Minimum of 8 years of leadership, people development, and operations experience
* Experience working in a Lean Manufacturing environment
* Experience developing effective and scalable operating systems and processes
* Proven track record of production process improvement and innovation
* Proven track record of managing complex change across large teams
* Proven track record of leading and developing others
* Proven ability to obtain project deliverables and company metrics
* Strong analytical thinking and organizational skills
* Strong written and verbal communication skills; Ability to learn quickly and transfer knowledge
* Requires standing for extended periods of time with frequent stretching, reaching, walking, stooping, pushing, and/or pulling in an environment that may be cold, hot, noisy, and wet and may have fumes or odors due to vehicle maintenance
* Ability to maintain high volume and high-quality content in a fast-paced environment.
* Ability to travel up to 80% (multi site responsibility)
* Ability to provide valuable and actionable feedback
* Proficient computer skills
* Must be at least 18 years of age
* Valid driver's license with a clean driving record (no DUIs and no more than two moving violations in the last 3 years).
* Ability to read, write, speak and understand English

This job description is not designed to contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Compensation Range: $120K-$140K annually

**Legal stuff** 
Hiring is contingent on passing a complete background check. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship. 
Carvana is an equal employment opportunity employer. All applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, national origin, age, mental or physical disability, protected veteran status, or genetic information, or any other basis protected by applicable law. Carvana also prohibits harassment of applicants or employees based on any of these protected categories.

**Oklahoma City, OK**
**Extremely Competitive Pay**
-

**Job Summary**
We are seeking an experienced quality leader to oversee and advance our quality management program within a growing aerospace manufacturing organization. This position plays a critical role in ensuring product integrity, maintaining customer and regulatory compliance, and driving continuous improvement throughout the company. Working closely with manufacturing, engineering, and executive leadership, the Director of Quality will lead quality initiatives, develop high-performing teams, strengthen organizational processes, and promote a culture of accountability and operational excellence. The ideal candidate combines strong technical knowledge with proven leadership skills and a commitment to delivering consistent, high-quality results.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities Include**

* Implement and maintain the company quality system in coordination with the Management Representative.
* Report on the performance of the quality system for review and as a basis for improvement of the quality system.
* Have knowledge and understanding of the standards and customer requirements against which the quality system is developed, maintained, and implemented.
* Provide leadership to subordinates, establishing goals and development plans to meet the strategic direction of the organization.
* Determine and enforce -- through functional groups - quality requirements in accordance with real company needs, based on current regulations and state-of-the art product development.
* Develop audit plans, select, and evaluate auditors, document non-conformance(s) and report non-conformances to management.
* Manage subordinate personnel and ensure proper documentation and methods used are according to the Quality Management System.
* Ensure employees are properly trained to perform their job duties in the manner expected, according to their specific job description.
* Establishes and maintains an effective system of communications throughout the organization.
* Represents the organization with major customers, shareholders, the financial community, and the public.

* Administer the company quality program in accordance with customer and company requirements.
* Ensure corrective and preventive actions are issued, responded, and completed.
* Promote continuous improvement initiatives for scrap reduction, reducing variation and waste, increasing profit and to improve product quality.
* Organize and promote companywide quality improvement efforts.
* Liaison with external parties on matters relating to the quality management system.
* Maintain the system for calibration of inspection, tools, and equipment for conformance to product specifications.
* Research and analyze data such as customer design proposals, specifications, quality requirements, and manuals to determine feasibility or processes or application and company’s ability to inspect product at the required stages of manufacture.
* Plan and direct quality activities and establishes QA priorities for keeping effective production operations and cost factors.
* Assist engineering in organizing and planning Quality Planning Meetings.
* Read and understand technical and non-technical documents that relate to contracts, purchasing, product design, manufacturing, and test. This includes the ability to interface with both technical and non-technical personnel.
* Evaluate, study, standardize and improve procedures for the assurance of quality, reliability, safety, and efficiency.
* Assess techniques for examining, questioning, evaluating, and reporting.
* Analyze inspection data to determine product conformance and process capability.
* Prepare composite reports from individual reports of subordinates.

* Assign duties and examine work for exactness, neatness, and conformance product specifications, policies and procedures.
* Coordinate and plan meetings with departments to develop documentation to support compliance to the applicable standards.

* Support the Quality Management System to assure compliance to quality, industrial and government standards and regulations and customer requirements.
* Adhere to all Quality Management System procedures and instructions.
* Maintain a safe, clean, and orderly work environment.
