existing_roles.description:
ShipMonk isn't just a 3PL — we're the tech-powered growth partner for ecommerce brands, running 12+ owned fulfillment centers across the US, Canada, the UK, and Europe so our merchants can stress less and grow more.

We are seeking a hands-on Director to join our Strategy & Operations team and lead high-impact initiatives that improve how ShipMonk works across departments. Reporting to our Senior Director of Strategy and Operations, you will take our most important cross-functional problems from a blank page to a deployed solution: framing the problem, defining success, building the answer, and proving the results. Your first major initiative will be transforming how we schedule, staff, and manage our hourly warehouse workforce.  
  
What you'll do:  
  
Lead Cross-Department Initiatives

* Lead major initiatives that improve processes across departments, especially where work, systems, and ownership break down between teams.
* Frame ambiguous problems, define the outcome, and work backward into a solution that teams actually adopt.
* Lead on-site discovery with leaders and frontline teams to understand how work really gets done.

Transform Workforce Management

* Lead the redesign of how we schedule, staff, and manage our hourly warehouse teams, starting from what the business needs to achieve.
* Pilot solutions in one fulfillment center and scale what works across our network.
* Track the outcomes that matter, such as labor cost, staffing coverage, and retention.

Drive Continuous Improvement

* Help the whole organization work better, improving quality, speed, and the employee and merchant experience, not just cost.
* Spot recurring friction across teams, prioritize the biggest opportunities, and help teams adopt improvements that last.
* Make structured problem solving a habit at every level of the organization.

Strengthen Our Governance

* Support the organization as it matures how it sets priorities, makes decisions, and follows through on commitments.
* Partner with leaders to build governance practices that fit how each team works rather than imposing one structure.
* Bring clear analysis and decision materials to executive discussions.

Analyze, Build, and Drive Adoption

* Analyze productivity, capacity, cost to serve, and profitability, and build models that quantify trade-offs and turn decisions into action.
* Prototype tools and workflows hands-on with AI tools such as Claude, and partner with Engineering and Data to take them to production.
* Spend meaningful time on-site, leading change management so improvements stick rather than fade after launch.

What you'll need:

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, business, supply chain, or a related field
* 3-5 years of experience in operations transformation, strategy, or management consulting, including leading implementations from requirements through deployment and adoption
* A track record of solving ambiguous, cross-functional problems with structured, KPI-driven thinking
* Experience leading process redesign and change management across departments; Lean, Six Sigma, or similar experience is a plus
* Strong analytical and financial modeling skills; SQL or BI experience is a plus
* A hands-on ownership style: comfortable on the warehouse floor and personally driving execution and adoption
* Experience building with AI tools such as Claude to prototype solutions
* Exposure to fulfillment, distribution, or manufacturing operations; workforce management experience is a plus
* Strong executive communication and the ability to influence without direct authority
* Ability to travel 25–35%, with more time on-site during discovery and rollouts

  + **Unrivaled Support:** We provide hands-on, "mom and pop" support with a global reach. Our dedicated teams are on-site at every fulfillment center, ready to jump into action.

  + **Committed to the Future:** We invest over $10 million annually in research and development to ensure our technology and services continually evolve, helping merchants plant roots with a partner who is here to stay.

**Our Core Values**

**Senior Manager of Operations**

**Scottsdale Mint | Casper, Wyoming**  
**Employment Type:** Full-Time | Salaried

**Company Summary**

Founded in 2008, Scottsdale Mint is a U.S.-based precious metals manufacturer recognized globally for its innovation, quality, and American craftsmanship. As a privately held producer of premium gold, silver, and platinum bullion, the company serves sovereign nations, central banks, Fortune 500 companies, industrial clients, and authorized distributors worldwide.

Operating from its advanced manufacturing facility in Casper, Wyoming, Scottsdale Mint specializes in high-purity bullion, legal-tender coin programs, and custom-branded precious metal products. The company combines artistic design, scientific precision, and advanced minting technology to deliver products recognized for their quality, detail, and authenticity.

**Position Summary**

The Senior Manager of Operations is responsible for overseeing the daily performance and overall effectiveness of Scottsdale Mint's Coining, Melting, CNC Machining, and Die Manufacturing departments. This position provides leadership and direction to approximately 30 employees, ensuring manufacturing operations are safe, efficient, productive, and aligned with company objectives.

The successful candidate will be a visible, hands-on leader capable of managing multiple manufacturing functions, developing departmental supervisors, establishing accountability, and improving operational performance while supporting current production requirements and future manufacturing growth.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Manufacturing & Operations Management**

* Oversee daily operations and production performance across Coining, Melting, CNC Machining, and Die Manufacturing.
* Establish departmental priorities, production goals, and performance expectations in coordination with senior management.
* Coordinate labor, equipment, and resources to maximize productivity, throughput, and manufacturing capacity.
* Monitor production schedules and workflow, identifying bottlenecks and implementing solutions to improve output and efficiency.
* Coordinate with Planning & Inventory Control, Fulfillment, Maintenance, Marketing, and other departments to support production requirements and company objectives.
* Develop, monitor, and report on departmental KPIs to optimize workforce utilization and ensure production schedule adherence.

**2. Leadership & Workforce Management**

* Provide leadership, direction, and accountability to departmental supervisors and employees.
* Manage staffing levels, scheduling, attendance, and labor allocation to meet production requirements.
* Establish clear expectations for employee performance, productivity, communication, and workplace conduct.
* Conduct performance reviews, address personnel matters, and establish development objectives for direct reports.
* Develop supervisory capabilities and ensure employees receive appropriate training to perform their responsibilities effectively.
* Foster a professional work environment emphasizing teamwork, accountability, ownership, and employee development.

**3. Safety, Compliance & Operational Excellence**

* Maintain consistent operating standards, manufacturing procedures, and a strong safety culture across all assigned departments.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA regulations, company safety policies, and applicable workplace requirements.
* Monitor key performance indicators, including production output, labor efficiency, downtime, quality, and schedule attainment.
* Evaluate manufacturing processes to identify safety concerns, operational inefficiencies, and opportunities for improvement.
* Promote proper equipment operation, preventative maintenance, housekeeping, and organization throughout manufacturing areas.
* Ensure operational and safety issues are addressed promptly and corrective actions are implemented.
* Communicate departmental performance, challenges, and improvement initiatives to senior management.

**Qualifications & Experience**

* 5–7 years of progressive manufacturing supervisory or management experience, preferably overseeing multiple departments.
* Experience managing production teams and workforces of approximately 25–50 employees preferred.
* Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Operations Management, or a related discipline preferred; equivalent practical experience will be considered.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, production workflows, labor management, and operational efficiency.
* Working knowledge of OSHA regulations and manufacturing safety requirements.
* Demonstrated ability to manage production objectives, develop supervisors, and hold employees accountable for performance.
* Strong organizational, problem-solving, and verbal and written communication skills.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and manufacturing-related reporting systems.

**Position Expectations**

The Senior Manager of Operations is expected to take ownership of the overall performance of the assigned manufacturing departments. This individual must provide consistent leadership, establish clear priorities, and ensure departmental supervisors are effectively managing their teams and achieving established objectives.

Success will be measured by the ability to meet production goals, maintain safe and efficient operations, effectively manage workforce resources, improve manufacturing performance, and develop a capable and accountable team.

existing_roles.description:
**Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality**

**Location:** Lakewood, Ohio  
**Company:** Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company  
**Employment Type:** Full Time  
**Reports To:** President

**About Ferry Cap**

Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company is a long-established American manufacturer of engineered fasteners and specialty metal components serving demanding industrial and power generation applications. As we invest in our people, equipment, and operating systems, we are seeking a senior quality leader who can help strengthen our processes and build a companywide culture of quality.

**Position Summary**

The Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality will lead Ferry Cap’s quality organization and serve as a key member of the company’s leadership team.

This is a hands on leadership position for someone with strong experience in metallurgy, metal transformation, manufacturing processes, and heat treatment. The successful candidate will work closely with operations, engineering, maintenance, supply chain, and customers to improve process control, solve technical problems, and ensure consistent product quality.

The right leader will view quality as an operating partnership, not simply an inspection function. This individual must be comfortable working on the production floor, engaging directly with employees, and helping build quality into every stage of the manufacturing process.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead all quality assurance, quality control, laboratory, inspection, and quality systems activities.
* Partner directly with operations to establish a culture in which safety, delivery, quality, and cost are shared responsibilities.
* Provide technical leadership related to metallurgy, raw materials, metal forming, metal transformation, machining, threading, and heat treatment.
* Oversee metallurgical testing and analysis, including hardness, microstructure, case depth, decarburization, mechanical properties, material certification, and failure analysis.
* Evaluate and improve heat treatment processes, including furnace controls, quenching, tempering, process consistency, and product conformance.
* Strengthen incoming, in process, and final inspection systems to ensure product requirements are consistently achieved.
* Lead root cause analysis and corrective action activities involving internal defects, customer complaints, supplier issues, and process failures.
* Use structured problem solving methods such as 8D, 5 Why, fishbone analysis, PFMEA, control plans, SPC, and MSA.
* Maintain and continuously improve the company’s quality management system, documentation, procedures, work instructions, and audit processes.
* Ensure compliance with customer requirements, industry standards, specifications, and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Lead customer audits, supplier audits, internal audits, and customer quality reviews.
* Build strong working relationships with customer quality and engineering teams.
* Develop meaningful quality metrics, including first pass yield, scrap, rework, cost of poor quality, customer complaints, corrective action effectiveness, and supplier performance.
* Improve material traceability and process control throughout the manufacturing operation.
* Lead supplier quality development and ensure purchased materials and outside processes meet Ferry Cap requirements.
* Develop, coach, and hold accountable the quality team while strengthening quality knowledge throughout the organization.
* Support new product introduction, process changes, capital projects, and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Establish clear containment, escalation, and corrective action processes when quality concerns arise.

**Required Qualifications**

* Significant quality leadership experience in a metal manufacturing environment.
* Strong practical knowledge of metallurgy, material properties, metal transformation, and heat treatment.
* Experience with manufacturing processes such as cold forming, forging, machining, threading, rolling, or similar metalworking operations.
* Demonstrated ability to diagnose metallurgical and manufacturing process failures.
* Experience leading quality systems, customer audits, corrective actions, and continuous improvement activities.
* Strong working knowledge of dimensional inspection, mechanical testing, metallurgical testing, calibration, and measurement systems.
* Experience using quality tools such as PFMEA, control plans, SPC, MSA, 8D, and root cause analysis.
* Proven ability to work collaboratively with operations and engineering teams.
* Strong leadership, communication, organization, and problem solving skills.
* Willingness to spend significant time on the manufacturing floor and become personally involved in resolving issues.
* Bachelor’s degree in metallurgy, materials science, engineering, manufacturing, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant manufacturing experience.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Ten or more years of progressive quality experience, including at least five years in a leadership role.
* Experience with engineered fasteners, high strength components, critical industrial products, or power generation applications.
* Experience with ISO based quality management systems and customer specific quality requirements.
* Experience working with commercial heat treat suppliers and internal heat treatment operations.
* ASQ certification, Six Sigma certification, or formal Lean manufacturing training.
* Experience working in a union manufacturing environment.

**Leadership Profile**

The successful candidate will be:

* Hands on and comfortable working directly with production employees.
* Collaborative and capable of building trust across departments.
* Technically strong, practical, and decisive.
* Focused on preventing defects instead of relying on inspection to find them.
* Comfortable challenging existing practices while respecting Ferry Cap’s people and history.
* Able to balance customer requirements with operational realities.
* Committed to accountability, continuous improvement, and developing others.

**Why Join Ferry Cap**

This position offers the opportunity to play a major role in the continued transformation and growth of a historic American manufacturing company. The Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality will have direct access to company leadership, meaningful influence over operations, and the opportunity to build a quality culture that supports Ferry Cap’s customers, employees, and long term success.

Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company is an equal opportunity employer. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs.

Our work is grounded in evidence-based strategies for adults and adolescents suffering from eating disorders. We work from a multi-disciplinary treatment team approach while integrating state-of-the-art medical, psychiatric, nutritional, and clinical strategies to provide comprehensive care within an intimate home setting.

The Director of Virtual Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for Monte Nido’s virtual programs in accordance with the organization’s philosophy and mission. Reporting to the Vice President of Virtual Programs, the Director leads the Program Manager and Group Facilitation Senior Manager, establishes consistent operating standards, and ensures effective coordination across program operations, group facilitation, clinical leadership, quality, compliance, and support functions. The role is accountable for staffing and capacity planning, scheduling and coverage, attendance and census processes, documentation and clinical quality oversight, regulatory readiness, performance measurement, process improvement, and resolution of escalated operational and safety concerns. The Director translates organizational priorities into reliable execution, develops leaders, uses data to identify risks and opportunities, and advances safe, high-quality, efficient virtual care.

Schedule: Monday-Friday

Salary: $75k-$85k annually plus bonus

Total Rewards::

Discover a rewarding career with us and enjoy an array of comprehensive benefits! We prioritize your success and well-being, providing:

* Competitive compensation
* Medical, dental, and vision insurance coverage (Benefits At a Glance)
* Retirement
* Company-paid life insurance, AD&D, and short-term disability
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
* Health Savings Account (HSA)
* Paid time off
* Professional development
* And many more!

We are committed to creating a diverse environment and are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

Responsibilities Include::

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**  
1. Provide strategic and operational leadership for virtual program operations, translating organizational priorities into clear plans, standards, and measurable outcomes.  
2. Lead, coach, and supervise the Program Manager/Coordinator and Group Facilitation Senior Manager, including goal setting, performance management, career development, succession planning, and corrective action when needed.  
3. Establish operating expectations across program administration and group facilitation, ensuring leaders maintain consistent practices for staffing, scheduling, coverage, attendance, documentation, client engagement, and escalation.  
4. Maintain oversight of staffing models, schedules, capacity, and coverage across virtual programs; anticipate resource needs and escalate material risks with clear recommendations.  
5. Own program schedules across virtual services, including schedule design, maintenance, and communication; identify availability limitations and escalate constraints that may affect access, coverage, or continuity of care to Clinical Directors and other appropriate clinical leaders.  
6. Oversee attendance, census, engagement, discharge, outcomes, client satisfaction, and operational performance indicators; use trends to improve retention, quality, and efficiency.  
7. Ensure reliable documentation and clinical quality audit processes, including timely corrective follow-up, retraining, chart completion, required signatures, and maintenance of program records.  
8. Direct operational readiness for Joint Commission, payer, licensing, and internal audits in partnership with clinical, quality, compliance, billing, and human resources leaders.  
9. Ensure virtual-program policies, procedures, care schedules, handbooks, workflows, and telehealth standards remain current, practical, and consistently implemented.  
10. Partner with clinical and medical leaders to resolve escalated client safety, attendance, staffing, documentation, and program-quality concerns while preserving appropriate clinical decision-making authority.  
11. Partner with Clinical Directors to develop and implement quality-of-care initiatives, monitor effectiveness, address identified gaps, and support consistent standards across virtual programs.  
12. Define performance expectations for operational functions and hold leaders accountable for employee development, engagement, conduct, productivity, and consistent application of policies in partnership with Human Resources.  
13. Lead cross-functional initiatives that improve workflows, technology use, communication, service quality, and the experience of clients, families, employees, and referral partners.  
14. Communicate significant operational, safety, quality, compliance, and resource risks to the Vice President of Virtual Programs with timely analysis and recommended actions.  
15. Represent virtual operations in required leadership and management meetings and facilitate decision-making, implementation, and follow-through across stakeholder groups.

**Additional Duties and Responsibilities**  
1. Support insurance, compliance, personnel-file, referral-partner, outpatient-provider, and discharge-transition activities when operational leadership is needed.  
2. Provide executive-ready updates on virtual program performance, risks, priorities, and improvement initiatives.  
3. Maintain professionalism, confidentiality, sound judgment, and respectful communication in all interactions.  
4. Adhere to Monte Nido & Affiliates policies, procedures, telehealth etiquette, and safety standards, and ensure assigned leaders reinforce them consistently.  
5. Provide additional operational leadership and complete other duties as assigned.  
6. VIRTUAL EMPLOYEES: We have the same expectations for employees as we do for Cares. We ask that you keep your camera on and join from a private space free of noise and distractions (e.g., not from a car) when meeting with Cares or joining a clinical staff meeting. You will need a reliable video conferencing setup, including a camera, microphone, and stable, high-speed Internet connection. You must also be prepared with a backup plan in the event of technology failures. We expect you to consider your personal appearance in much the same way you would when seeing Cares in person. You must also keep your background clean and professional.

Qualifications::

* Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, behavioral health, business, or a related field required; master’s degree preferred. An equivalent combination of education and directly relevant leadership experience may be considered.
* Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in behavioral health, healthcare operations, or a comparable care-delivery environment, including at least three years of people leadership. Experience leading managers, overseeing virtual operations, managing multi-program workflows, and supporting accreditation, payer, and regulatory requirements is strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated ability to lead and develop managers, establish clear expectations, and drive accountability across multiple programs and functions
* Strong operational judgment, change leadership, project management, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
* Ability to interpret operational and quality data, identify trends, manage risk, and implement sustainable improvements.
* Knowledge of Joint Commission standards, payer requirements, patient confidentiality laws, telehealth requirements, and organizational compliance expectations.

existing_roles.description:
Your Contribution
=================

The Head of Plant Production Engineering is responsible for leading all Production Engineering activities associated with customer projects, product acquisitions, new product launches, industrialization, and production readiness within the plant. This position serves as the plant's primary owner for Production Engineering processes, ensuring successful execution of the Product Development Process (PDP) from acquisition through Start of Production (SOP) and ramp-up. The role provides leadership to Production Engineers, drives standardization and deployment of manufacturing concepts, ensures manufacturability of product designs, manages capital investments, and represents Operations within project core teams. The Plant Head of Production Engineering ensures project launches meet safety, quality, delivery, cost, and operational performance objectives.

* Lead, develop, coach, & manage the plant Production Engineering organization.
* Build organizational capability to support current and future product launches.
* Own industrialization activities for all customer projects within the plant. Ensure successful execution of product launches from acquisition and business transfer through SOP and stabilization.
* Lead development of manufacturing concepts, production processes, line layouts, and assembly strategies.
* Ensure product designs are manufacturable and meet operational standards.
* Coordinate launch readiness across Manufacturing Engineering, Tooling Engineering, Quality, Logistics, Purchasing, and Operations Support acquisition reviews and participate in PAC, PRC, and pre-development activities.
* Ensure implementation of Design-for-Manufacturing principles throughout project development. Ensure compliance with MAHLE PDP milestones, gates, deliverables, and timing requirements. Oversee completion of all Production Engineering deliverables throughout all quality gates.
* Monitor project status, risks, cost performance, capacity requirements, and launch readiness. Lead escalation activities when project risks threaten timing, quality, or cost objectives. Review project dashboards and launch metrics with plant leadership and program teams.
* Approve and govern: Manufacturing concepts, Process flows, Plant layouts, Assembly concepts, Material flow strategies, Value stream integration.
* Ensure application of Lean Manufacturing and Manufacturing Optimization Process (MOP) methodologies in alignment with Operations Excellence Manager.
* Drive takt-time analysis, line balancing, ergonomic studies, and capacity planning. Validate cycle times using MTM or equivalent engineering methods. Ensure implementation of standardized manufacturing processes across the region.
* Ensure development, completion, and approval of Process FMEA (P-FMEA), Control Plans, Special Characteristics, Process Capability Studies, Validation Plans. Support flawless launch activities and manufacturing risk reduction. Lead readiness reviews for installation checks, internal process approval, internal run at rate, customer run at rate, PPAP readiness. Ensure production systems consistently achieve quality and operational KPI’s.
* Lead capital expenditure planning and approval activities. Validate business cases and investment requirements. Ensure optimal utilization of existing equipment before requesting new capital. Support supplier selection through PDC and SDC processes. Approve manufacturing equipment specifications. Participate in procurement and acceptance of production equipment, tooling, fixtures, and test systems.
* Chair Production Engineering project meetings, and lead the plant Production Engineering Extended Team, ensuring effective communication between Project Core Teams and Plant Extended Teams.

Your Experience & Qualifications

* Bachelor’s Degree required, B.S. in Engineering, or related technical discipline required. Master’s Degree preferred.
* 8+ years’ experience in manufacturing, launch, industrialization, or production engineering.
* 5+ years’ progressive leadership responsibility regarding engineering or manufacturing operations.
* Demonstrated success in leading complex product launches and PDP projects.
* Experience in an automotive manufacturing facility required; high volume, medium to large campus experience preferred.
* Demonstrated knowledge in IATF16949, ISO14001 and 45001 Audits and processes.
* Excellent diagnostic abilities / root cause analysis required; Lean Six Sigma and Black Belt certification strongly preferred.

Our Offer

We will provide a collaborative environment working on exciting assignments, along with ongoing personal & career development opportunities. We encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every single requirement. You may just be the right candidate for this or other roles! After receiving your online application, the interview process will typically be, a screening call followed by Personal Interview(s).

  

#DiversityMatters with our inclusive culture, we welcome applications from all social, religious & ethnical backgrounds, disabilities both mental and physical, identities (gender) and neurodivergent people.

protected_roles.title: Quality Director
protected_roles.description:
As the
**Director of Quality**
, you will lead the quality strategy and continuous improvement efforts across all Bison manufacturing sites. You will be responsible for ensuring that the products meet or exceed customer expectations, industry standards, and regulatory requirements while driving overall quality performance and fostering a culture of continuous improvement. You will work closely with cross-functional teams to establish and maintain effective quality systems, drive process improvements, and ensure compliance with industry certifications.
  
  
This position can be based at either our
**Whitsett, NC**
or
**Reynosa, MX**
facility.
  
  
**What You Will Do**
  
  

* Leadership & Strategy

+ Develop and execute a strategic quality plan in alignment with business unit goals.
+ Lead, mentor, and develop a team of quality professionals across two locations, ensuring consistency in processes and objectives.
+ Champion a culture of quality, accountability, and continuous improvement.

* Quality Management Systems (QMS)

+ Oversee the implementation, maintenance, and improvement of the QAD Elements QMS and other relevant Quality Management Systems at both locations. Ensure compliance with customer, regulatory, and industry-specific quality standards (e.g., FDA, ISO, AS9100, etc.).
+ Monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of quality management systems and propose enhancements to improve overall performance.

* Process & Product Quality

+ Collaborate with sales, operations, engineering, and supply chain teams to identify drive resolution of quality issues, ensuring process and product integrity.
+ Support root cause analysis and drive corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) for internal and external quality issues.
+ Oversee first article inspections, process capability studies, and validation/qualification activities to ensure robust manufacturing processes.

* Continuous Improvement

+ Lead Lean Six Sigma or other continuous improvement initiatives aimed at reducing defects, enhancing efficiency, and improving overall quality.
+ Implement data-driven decision-making tools (e.g., SPC, FMEA, Control Plans) to monitor and improve process capabilities.
+ Facilitate cross-functional value stream mapping sessions and quality workshops to drive process improvements.

* Customer & Supplier Relations

+ Serve as the main point of contact for customer quality issues, audits, and feedback, ensuring timely and effective resolution.
+ Oversee supplier quality management, including audits, performance monitoring, and supplier development initiatives.

* Metrics & Reporting

+ Establish and track key performance indicators (KPIs) related to quality performance, including scrap/rework, defect rates, customer complaints, and audit findings.
+ Regularly report quality performance metrics to senior leadership, highlighting trends and recommending corrective actions.

* Regulatory Compliance & Audits

+ Lead internal and external audits, ensuring the sites comply with relevant standards and certifications.
+ Ensure the manufacturing facilities are audit-ready at all times and coordinate responses to audit findings.

**What We Are Looking For**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Quality Management, or a related field. Master’s degree preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in quality management within a manufacturing environment, with at least 5 years in a leadership role.
* Demonstrated experience with quality management systems (ISO 9001, AS9100, FDA, or equivalent) and continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma).
* Demonstrated ability and willingness to use AI tools to improve productivity, decision-making, work quality, and to reduce costs. The successful candidate must be able to identify appropriate AI use cases and critically evaluate AI-generated outputs.
* Proven track record of driving quality improvements across multi-site operations.
* Ability to travel as needed to the BU manufacturing sites (up to 30%)
* Strong leadership and team-building skills.
* Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities.
* Ability to communicate effectively with all levels of the organization.
* Proficiency in quality tools such as SPC, FMEA, 8D, and Root Cause Analysis.

**Compensation**
Employee Type: Salaried
  
  
Currency: USD
  
  
Salary Minimum: 135,000
  
  
Salary Maximum: 185,000
  
  
Incentive: Yes
  
  
Disclaimer: Where a specific pay range is noted, it is a good faith estimate at the time of this posting. The actual salary offered will be based on experience, skills, qualifications, market / business considerations, and geographic location.
  
  
For more information on AMETEK's competitive benefits, please click here.
  
  
AMETEK, Inc. is a leading global provider of industrial technology solutions serving a diverse set of attractive niche markets with annual sales over $7.5 billion.
  
  
AMETEK is committed to making a safer, sustainable, and more productive world a reality. We use differentiated technology solutions to solve our customers’ most complex challenges. We employ 22,000 colleagues, in 35 countries, that are grounded by our core values: Ethics and Integrity, Respect for the Individual, Inclusion, Teamwork, and Social Responsibility. AMETEK is a component of the S&P 500. Visit https://www.ametek.com/careers for more information.

protected_roles.description:
**About Analog Devices**
Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI ) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, and software technologies into solutions that help drive advancements in digitized factories, mobility, and digital healthcare, combat climate change, and reliably connect humans and the world. With revenue of more than $9 billion in FY24 and approximately 24,000 people globally, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible™. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and Twitter (X).
  
  
**Senior Manager, Production – Fab Operations**
The Camas Wafer Fab is a growing 150mm, high‑volume, 24x7 manufacturing facility producing leading‑edge precision ICs in support of ADI’s diversified semiconductor business.
  
  
Reporting to the Wafer Fab General Manager, the
**Senior Manager, Production – Fab Operations**
will lead our ~300‑employee Production organization—including Production Managers, Supervisors, Trainers, 5S & Continuous Improvement, New Product Technicians, Leads, and Operators—who execute day‑to‑day manufacturing, testing, and shipping of a broad product portfolio as the fab continues to ramp, expand, and modernize a facility with over 25 years of operational history.
  
  
Apply now for the opportunity to grow your career and help innovate ahead of what’s possible.
  
  
**Job Duties**
The Senior Manager, Production – Fab Operations is a senior operations leader responsible for translating site strategy into strong operational execution. Responsibilities are aligned to three core competency areas:
  
  
**Operational & Strategic Execution**

* Translate site and enterprise manufacturing strategies into actionable operational plans for the Production organization, aligned with objectives for safety, quality, productivity, cost, talent development, and sustainability.
* Lead the execution of production improvement roadmaps, supporting longer‑term digital transformation, automation, and modernization initiatives defined at the site level.
* Drive adoption of data‑driven and AI‑enabled decision making within production operations, leveraging analytics, automation, and machine‑learning‑based insights to improve daily execution and performance stability.
* Support change management efforts associated with new technologies, digital tools, demand shifts, and new product introductions, ensuring disciplined adoption on the production floor.
* Share and apply best‑known methods from across ADI’s manufacturing network to continuously elevate production performance.

**Operational Excellence**

* Maintain a safe and healthy work environment by enforcing organizational standards, adhering to 5S principles, and complying with ADI policies, legal requirements, and regulatory standards.
* Own day‑to‑day production quality performance, applying a zero‑defect mindset using traditional quality methodologies (8D, 5‑Why, SPC) and AI‑assisted defect detection, yield analysis, and trend identification.
* Lead execution of production plans that deliver short‑term tactical results while driving continuous improvement across Safety, Quality, Productivity, Cost, and Efficiency metrics.
* Utilize predictive and prescriptive analytics, where applicable, to anticipate equipment issues, process drift, capacity constraints, and safety risks before they impact performance.
* Provide clear tactical direction through written reports, dashboards, presentations, daily operational reviews, all‑hands meetings, and shift‑level stand‑ups, ensuring decisions are grounded in accurate, timely data.
* Lead capacity modeling, scenario analysis, and demand response activities within the production organization, partnering with site leadership on longer‑range planning.
* Partner closely with Supply Chain to optimize wafer starts, cycle time, and scheduling, balancing customer demand with fab constraints and operational risk.
* Participate in internal and external audits to ensure compliance, business continuity, and continuous improvement, including adherence to ADI’s responsible and ethical use of AI in manufacturing operations.
* Support the development and ramp of new products and non‑standard fabrication requirements while maintaining safe, stable, and predictable production output.
* Ensure effective cross‑training programs and skills matrices are in place, leveraging digital tools to improve workforce flexibility and readiness.

**Effective Team Leadership**

* Lead recruiting, hiring, onboarding, and training efforts for the Production organization, aligning staffing plans with quarterly and longer‑range production needs.
* Foster a culture of engagement, accountability, and continuous improvement through proactive communication, coaching, and visible leadership presence across all shifts.
* Develop production supervisors and frontline leaders capable of operating in an increasingly digital, automated, and data‑driven manufacturing environment.
* Execute effective performance management processes to improve team continuity, leadership capability, and operational results.
* Partner with Human Resources to support competency development, technical capability building, and training plans aligned with future manufacturing needs.
* Ensure alignment with ADI Enterprise Excellence Guiding Principles, emphasizing safety, quality, operational rigor, and responsible innovation.

**SCHEDULE**
This is an exempt role, working on‑site in Camas, Washington, primarily Monday through Friday, supporting a 24x7 continuous operation.
  
  
Occasional night or weekend hours are required to support operational needs.
  
  
**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, or a related field required; technical or engineering degree strongly preferred.
* 8+ years of leadership experience in high‑volume wafer fabrication or advanced manufacturing operations.
* Demonstrated success leading large production teams through supervisors and frontline leaders.
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with proven effectiveness in a data‑driven, metrics‑based operating environment.
* Solid working knowledge of manufacturing and business systems (ERP/MRP, MES, dispatching, capacity planning, Microsoft Office).
* Demonstrated ability to apply analytics, digital tools, and emerging AI/ML capabilities to improve safety, quality, productivity, and cost performance.
* Strong problem‑solving skills, operational discipline, and passion for continuous improvement.

*For positions requiring access to technical data, Analog Devices, Inc. may have to obtain export licensing approval from the U.S. Department of Commerce - Bureau of Industry and Security and/or the U.S. Department of State - Directorate of Defense Trade Controls. As such, applicants for this position – except US Citizens, US Permanent Residents, and protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) – may have to go through an export licensing review process.*
*Analog Devices is an equal opportunity employer. We foster a culture where everyone has an opportunity to succeed regardless of their race, color, religion, age, ancestry, national origin, social or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, marital status, pregnancy, parental status, disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, union membership, and political affiliation, or any other legally protected group.*
*EEO is the Law: Notice of Applicant Rights Under the Law.*
Job Req Type: Experienced
  
  
Required Travel: No
  
  
Shift Type: 1st Shift/Days
  
  
The expected wage range for a new hire into this position is $143,200 to $196,900.
  
  

* Actual wage offered may vary depending on work location, experience, education, training, external market data, internal pay equity, or other bona fide factors.
* This position qualifies for a discretionary performance-based bonus which is based on personal and company factors
* This position includes medical, vision and dental coverage, 401k, paid vacation, holidays, and sick time, and other benefits.
* Benefits for the position includes 10 paid holidays per year, paid vacation starting at 136 hours per year for full-time employees (prorated for part-time employees), and paid sick time that exceeds the requirements of the Washington State Sick Leave law.

**Bring more to life.**
Are you ready to accelerate your potential and make a real difference within life sciences, diagnostics and biotechnology?
  
  
At Beckman Coulter Life Sciences, one of Danaher’s 15+ operating companies, our work saves lives—and we’re all united by a shared commitment to innovate for tangible impact.
  
  
You’ll thrive in a culture of belonging where you and your unique viewpoint matter. And by harnessing Danaher’s system of continuous improvement, you help turn ideas into impact – innovating at the speed of life.
  
  
At Beckman Coulter Life Sciences, we know time is the most critical facet in the laboratory today:  time to get life-saving therapies to patients faster; reclaiming time by automating tedious manual workflows; and saving time spent addressing erroneous or complex results.
  
  
We are partners in time and accelerate answers to critical questions through the power of automation. We develop innovations for scientists by scientists, with many of our 3,300+ global colleagues coming from the laboratory.
  
  
It’s all part of our time-tested approach to bringing meaningful innovations at the speed of life since 1935. And we’re just beginning. Working together, let’s put our time and talents together to advance human health for tomorrow.
  
  
Learn about the Danaher Business System which makes everything possible.
  
  
The
**Senior Manager - Global New Product Introduction (NPI)**
- Systems Hardware is responsible for leading Manufacturing Engineering and Operations readiness for hardware- and systems-based product development programs across Beckman Coulter Life Sciences' global manufacturing network. This leader serves as the critical bridge between R&D, Product Management, Supply Chain, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Service, and Manufacturing Operations to ensure successful design transfer, manufacturing scale-up, and on-time commercialization of complex life science instrumentation.
  
  
This position reports to the Director, Manufacturing Engineering and is part of the Global Manufacturing Engineering & Innovation organization located in Indianapolis, Indiana. This will be an on-site role with global collaboration across U.S., China, and Europe BEC LS manufacturing and development locations as required.
  
  
**In This Role, You Will Have The Opportunity To**

* Lead Manufacturing Engineering engagement from product concept through commercialization for hardware and instrument platforms, ensuring safety, quality, delivery, cost, supply continuity, reliability, capacity, and launch objectives are achieved.
* Lead governance for the global hardware NPI portfolio, including milestones, resource prioritization, capital plans, risk management, escalation paths, launch metrics, executive reviews, and post-launch stabilization.
* Partner with the Director, Manufacturing Engineering to develop and deploy global NPI and manufacturing engineering strategies aligned with business growth, product roadmaps, manufacturing footprint, capacity, lifecycle, and innovation priorities.
* Ensure robust design transfer and manufacturing readiness across U.S., China, and Europe locations, including manufacturing requirements, process development, equipment and tooling, pilot builds, test methods, documentation, process validation, production ramp, and issue closure.
* Drive Design for Manufacturing, Assembly, Test, Service, Reliability, and Cost in partnership with R&D and other functions, using the Danaher Business System, standard work, visual management, value stream mapping, daily management, kaizen, and structured problem solving.
* Lead selected global manufacturing excellence initiatives involving engineering standards, process capability, automation, digital manufacturing, manufacturing technology, test strategy, productivity, value engineering, and continuous cost improvement.
* Lead and develop managers, engineers, and technical project leaders across a global matrix; strengthen accountability, technical capability, talent reviews, succession planning, leadership development, inclusion, and mobility across global and site teams.

**The Essential Requirements Of The Job Include**

* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Biomedical, Electrical, Manufacturing, Systems, or a closely related engineering discipline.
* Typically 10+ years of progressive experience across engineering, manufacturing, operations, product development, and/or new product introduction.
* At least 5 years of people leadership experience, with demonstrated ability to lead managers, engineers, or technical project leaders across locations or in a global matrix. Working knowledge of FDA, ISO, quality-system, design-control, risk-management, verification and validation, change-control, traceability, process-validation, and product-lifecycle requirements.
* Demonstrated success launching complex electromechanical, software-enabled, diagnostic, medical device, or life science instrumentation products in regulated manufacturing environments.
* Deep experience with design transfer, industrialization, manufacturing readiness, process development and validation, manufacturing test, tooling and equipment, supplier readiness, ramp, and lifecycle support.
* Proven ability to translate business and product strategy into engineering priorities, operating mechanisms, investment recommendations, and measurable results. Experience leading portfolio governance, resource prioritization, capital planning, risk reviews, and cross-functional executive decision-making.

**It would be a plus if you also possess previous experience in:**

* Master’s degree in engineering, an MBA, PMP certification, Lean Six Sigma certification, or comparable advanced development.
* Experience with flow cytometry, centrifugation, liquid handling, particle characterization, genomics, bioprocessing, or comparable scientific instrumentation platforms.
* Experience leading global engineering transformation, automation, digital manufacturing, connected equipment, manufacturing data systems, or advanced analytics initiatives.
* Experience with site transfers, localization, manufacturing footprint changes, contract manufacturers, supplier development, acquisition integration, or rapid capacity expansion.

Beckman Coulter Life Sciences, a Danaher operating company, offers a broad array of comprehensive, competitive benefit programs that add value to our lives. Whether it’s a health care program or paid time off, our programs contribute to life beyond the job. Check out our benefits at Danaher Benefits Info.
  
  
We offer comprehensive package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance and 401(k) to eligible employees.
  
  
Join our winning team today. Together, we’ll accelerate the real-life impact of tomorrow’s science and technology. We partner with customers across the globe to help them solve their most complex challenges, architecting solutions that bring the power of science to life.

**About Us**
Spellman High Voltage Electronics Corporation, a family owned business for over 75 years, takes pride in powering progress in health, security and quality of life. We are key partners with the world’s leading medical devices, semiconductor, scientific analytics and industrial systems manufacturers. When they want to push the limits of what’s possible with high voltage applications, they turn to us to make it happen.
  
  
While Spellman is not a household name, our products are used to make and often power many of the most advanced technologies that make modern life possible. With design and manufacturing sites in North America, Europe and Asia, we have become the preferred provider of high voltage power solutions for OEMs pushing the boundaries of technology around the world by designing and producing the products they need to power progress.
  
  
The primary role of the Senior Manager, NPI will provide leadership to a diverse team of engineers and provide support in the design, documentation, analysis, and coordination of release for products being transferred from design to production. The Senior Manager, NPI will contribute to the success of projects as well as the team. In this role, the Senior Manager, NPI will balance the work within the team, coach the team through technical challenges, and act as a role model in the organization. The Senior Manager, NPI will be expected to provide technical input to the leadership team to support business decisions.
  
  
This leader, with their team develops and implements operations requirements for design transfer across all product portfolios and collaborates with development, manufacturing and technical support teams to assure that all aspects of design for quality and manufacturability (DQM) are utilized for robust design development, transfer and ultimately scale up. Assures appropriate test method validations and product specifications are developed and implemented. Individual is also responsible for managing new part number creation and appropriate work instruction development. Will work cross functionally to ensure repeatability and reproducibility of the manufactured products within product and process capabilities and meeting of desired specifications.
  
  
Provides leadership of design transfer activities of products also engages in technology transfer activities involving product end of life or transfer to other Spellman High Voltage Electronics manufacturing sites.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Establishes overall team direction and goals, and sets direction of resources toward completion of goals, in conjunction with Senior Leadership in both Development and Operations. Promotes an open, collaborative environment focused on teamwork
* Establishes and maintains design transfer project milestones and timelines
* Supports robust design specification development and validation activities during design transfer, working closely with counterparts in the development team.
* Oversight for all NPI deliverables to the customer and expected team output
* Communication with all members of the NPI team to monitor project status, scope changes, and KPIs
* Work with the Product Development teams to ensure that all new products have been put through the adequate testing and best practices have been used
* Work collaboratively with peers and other cross-functional team members including define sub-system design requirement specifications and design architectures
* Manage and collaborate across multi-technical disciplines and cross-functional teams
* Plan, manage, and delegate project resource requirements, schedules, and task activities.
* Resolve problems using solutions that involve new techniques, technologies, or concepts.
* Effective application of engineering excellence processes and techniques (DFMEA, PFMEA, DOE, DVP&R, boundary diagrams, DFM/A, Technical Design Reviews, fault tree and risk assessment, SCRUM, etc.)
* Lead a team of NPI Manufacturing Engineers, in collaboration with other organizations, to support production of complex products with responsibilities including but not limited to:
* Establish group and individual objectives, priorities, and metrics
* Ensure production of products meets expected output
* Ensure quality requirements are fulfilled and maintained
* Provide technical support for failure analysis and root cause investigation of product failures.
* Analyze manufacturing lines from a risk perspective (pFMEA) to incorporate and validate critical tests used in manufacturing.
* Assume responsibility for the validation of manufacturing equipment and processes leveraging standard qualification approaches (IQ/OQ/PQ/DQ/PPQ).
* Provide production line support for day-to-day engineering issues on production and NPI lines.
* Identify and implement continuous improvement projects with respect to first pass yield, cycle time reduction, product reliability, capacity enhancements, and cost reduction.
* Liaise between project management, engineering, and manufacturing functions to ensure project goals are on track
* Adherence to applicable QMS policies and procedures
* Ensure the team sets and meets reasonable deliverable expectations Review and approve engineering changes
* Facilitate problem-solving efforts and continually improve processes
* Understand, lead, and coach in DFX concepts, pFMEA, problem-solving, and transfer efforts
* Lead in the decision-making process for production planning and layout
* Evaluate and estimate the required and proposed engineering tasks (headcount or hours) Understand the product funnel and needs for NPI resources during the early phases of development
* Other duties as assigned by management

**Requirements**

* Minimum of 15 years of demonstrated experience in people management and leadership role
* Minimum of 10 years experience in electronics manufacturing and knowledge of Design Control guidelines
* Minimum of 10 years leading/managing New Product Introduction Teams; including hiring, employee development, managing subordinate managers, project planning, and coordination in a matrixed organization
* Strong Conflict resolution and negotiation skills
* Strong written and verbal communication skills
* Excellent time management, planning, organization and problem solving skills
* Demonstrated ability to lead, mentor and coach team members
* Effective communication and interpersonal skills to interact effectively with all levels of the organization as well as directly with key customer contacts
* Must be very good with materials, mechanical parts and electronic components logistics, planning, well organized and resourceful;
* Must be able to multitask in an environment requirement a high level of detail and accuracy, work independently with guidance and take ownership of all assigned tasks;
* Capable of presenting information to management team and influencing key stakeholders;
* Ability to relentlessly track and follow-up on open issues and action items;
* Prior responsibility for validation of processes, equipment, and products.
* Experience in an ISO 13485, ISO 9001, or medical device manufacturing environment preferred.
* A clear understanding of BOM, BOM structure, ECO process, and materials/product setup

Our good faith estimate of the salary range for this role is $155,000 - $170,000. Exact compensation may vary based on skills, experience, and other factors. In addition to base pay, we offer a full benefits package.
  
  
This position requires on-site presence at Spellman High Voltage headquarters in Hauppauge, NY.

protected_roles.title: Director, Continuous Improvement
protected_roles.description:
**Position Summary**
Assist with development of Corporate Improvement strategies and carry out transformation and strategy deployment within business area. Based on Corporate Continuous Improvement strategies, develop lean strategy applicable to the business to enable execution. Influence and coach senior management and their teams on Business transformation, cultural change, engagement, Lean tool adoption, and empowerment, with a passionate approach to results. Drive results through the use of common metrics and data in various areas of the organization including those with environments of ambiguity. Provide coaching, training, and lead management workshops on principles of continuous improvement, cultural transformation, and leadership mindset. Demonstrated ability to coach VP and SVP levels of Executive Management on Transformation.
  
  
**50-75% domestic and international travel**
**What You’ll Do As a Director Continuous Improvement**

* Organize senior management CI/lean steering committee and activities to set direction for business transformation and provide guidance to execute. Ensures that all local steering committees are supported and operate effectively.
* Collaborate with business leaders to facilitate and lead cultural and strategic changes across functional departmental boundaries within designated business area.
* Advise and counsel leadership by providing strategic direction in prioritizing CI opportunities and ensuring that CI initiatives align with the business strategy.
* Develop and implement a team-based learning environment along with the appropriate structure to sustain improvements.
* Create and implement transformation plans across the organization based on Corporate Continuous Improvement strategy, and local business strategy, and directly manage CI initiatives and programs.
* Drive Continuous Improvement implementation to achieve cost reductions, cycle time improvements, and quality improvements through effective Lean tool management, benchmarking, Key Performance Indicator development, and scorecard development and monitoring for various functions within the organization.
* Develops and leads team to apply structured, technical problem solving methodologies such as DMAIC, six sigma green belt/black belt, statistical data analysis, etc. to confirm root causes of problems, in alignment with strategic needs.
* Assesses, coaches, and provides constructive feedback to teams to strengthen competencies within the enterprise.
* Implement methods to identify Continuous Improvement opportunities within the organization through the use of key metrics, analysis, accountability, and standardization.
* Provides advice and consultation as a transformation subject matter expert on best practices, significant projects, and/or special Continuous Improvement initiatives.
* Drives team to implement corrective and preventative actions to solve root causes and prevent recurrence, reduce variation, and drive improvement in quality and other key KPIs.
* Prepares budgets, schedules, and other financial reports for successful strategy deployment.
* Hires, trains, develops, coaches, and provides team member guidance and supervision in the event of having direct report(s).
* Maintain professional and technical knowledge through benchmarking world-class organizations and personal Continuous Improvement and Business Transformation related training.
* Drives and coaches use of project management principles including establishing and tracking timelines, identifying, and mitigating risks, communicating across teams at all levels.
* Other assigned duties.

**Required**
**The Experience, Skills, and Abilities Needed**

* Bachelor’s Degree (Engineering, Supply Chain and Logistics, or other Technical Field)
* Minimum 15 years of demonstrated qualified Improvement experience in a leadership role.
* One successful enterprise transformation required with experience in deploying lean culture in an organization.
* Minimum 8 years’ experience leading and managing a Continuous Improvement team.
* Demonstrated impact that translates to clear, bottom line performance results with step-function change with ability to produce $3 million in cost savings.
* Strong analytical skills and understanding of problem-solving techniques. Proficiency in analyzing business needs, determining appropriate solutions and/or opportunities, and deploying them.
* Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to influence, communicate, motivate, instill confidence, and persuade in difficult or complex situations.
* Demonstrated impact using improvement tools: For example, Toyota Productions System and methodologies such as: A3 Development and Management, Process Flow Mapping, 5S/Visual Factory, TPM, QCO-SMED, Standard Work, Process Problem Solving, Built In Quality, Just In Time, Kaizen/Continuous Improvement, Chaku-chaku lines, karikuri devices, DMAIC, Six Sigma Green Belt/Black Belt, statistical data analysis, etc.
* Lean certification from a recognized independent technical organization.
* Experience with improvement leadership in large functional areas i.e., Field Service, R&D, Plant Operations, Administrative Operations, etc.
* Experience delivering training, coaching, and developing all levels: executive to hourly employees.

**Preferred**

protected_roles.title: Director of Continuous Improvement
protected_roles.description:
Restek is looking for a builder. As our Director of Continuous Improvement, you’ll stand up an enterprise-wide continuous improvement program, developing the systems, the talent, and the Lean culture that make operational excellence part of how we work every day across Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Engineering, and Customer Experience.

Reporting to the Vice President of Operations, you’ll be our principal change agent, leading everything from multi-year transformation programs to focused Kaizen events. Your work will directly shape our strategic priorities by reducing waste and scrap, raising quality, speeding flow, improving the customer experience, and growing profitability.

**What You’ll Do**

Set the Strategy

* Own the multi-year CI roadmap, aligned with Restek’s strategic plan, annual operating plan, and Operations priorities.
* Establish the management system that makes improvement stick (daily management, tiered huddles, A3 problem solving) and define a CI maturity model to guide each function’s progress.
* Partner with Finance to validate savings and ensure improvement gains show up in the P&L.

Lead the Work

* Personally lead and facilitate high-impact Kaizen events, Value Stream Mapping, and transformation projects tied to safety, quality, delivery, cost, inventory, and customer outcomes.
* Drive measurable gains in OEE, first-pass yield, scrap and rework, on-time delivery, lead time, inventory turns, customer response time, and total cost of quality.
* Make sure improvement work is well scoped, resourced, and sustained, and bring the best practices from inside and outside Restek to every team.

Make an Impact Across the Business

* **Manufacturing:**
  Improve safety, quality, throughput, changeover, and productivity through standard work, visual management, and a Lean production system.
* **Customer Experience:**
  Help deliver an industry-leading experience through faster response and resolution, better processes, and digital enablement.
* **Supply Chain:**
  Strengthen supplier quality and delivery, optimize inventory, and streamline order-to-cash, delivering measurable cost savings.
* **Engineering:**
  Partner on design for manufacturability, new product introduction, and change management to speed time-to-market and build it right the first time.

Build Capability and Culture

* Build, lead, and develop the Continuous Improvement team.
* Design and deliver Restek’s CI training curriculum, including Lean fundamentals, Yellow/Green/Black Belt paths, problem-solving methods, and leader standard work.
* Coach senior leaders and frontline managers in CI thinking, and develop change agents at every level to scale CI beyond the central team.
* Put the metrics and dashboards in place that make progress visible from the manufacturing floor to the executive team, and share wins and learnings across the organization.

**How We Lead at Restek**

Restek leaders model our core values and act as stewards of our culture. They communicate openly, build trust, and support the growth and well-being of their teams. They think globally and act locally, create clarity around goals, hold themselves accountable, partner across functions and regions, and lead with humility and service so every employee-owner can contribute to Restek’s success.

**What You Bring**

**Qualifications:**

The typical requirements for this role include a bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration (master's degree, preferred), or a related field, plus 10 years of progressive operations and CI experience, including at least 5 years in a senior CI or operational excellence leadership role in manufacturing, or the equivalent combination of education and experience.

**Additional Skills & Abilities:**

* A proven track record of leading enterprise-level Lean transformations with sustained, financially validated results.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt certification (Master Black Belt certification is preferred)
* Hands-on experience across multiple functions (manufacturing, supply chain, quality, customer service, and/or engineering), with credibility on the manufacturing floor and with leadership.
* Experience leading and developing CI practitioners and managers.
* Deep fluency in the CI toolkit: Lean (5S, standard work, visual management, flow, pull, SMED, TPM, Kaizen), Six Sigma (DMAIC, SPC, DOE), Value Stream Mapping, Hoshin Kanri, and structured problem solving (A3, 8D, 5-Why, fishbone).
* Advanced Excel and Power BI (or equivalent) skills for data-driven decision making.
* A servant-leader and coach who thinks strategically, executes in detail, and influences from the manufacturing floor to the Leadership Team, with outstanding written, verbal, and executive presentation skills.

Experience in a regulated manufacturing environment (e.g., FDA, ISO 9001, ISO 13485, GMP) or in scientific instruments, life sciences, chromatography, analytical, or precision-manufactured products and experience bringing digital tools and analytics (e.g., MES, ERP, Power BI, advanced analytics) into the CI toolkit is preferred.

This full onsite position will require the successful completion of a standard background check in accordance with Restek policy. Employment with Restek will require successful completion of a pre-employment drug screen.

**What Makes Restek Unique**

We prioritize work-life balance and well-being with offerings like generous PTO, unlimited sick time, onsite fitness center and wellness program with incentives, childcare reimbursement, and adoption assistance—giving you the tools to Own Your Well-Being. Through our Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) and robust 8% retirement contributions, you can Own Your Financial Future while sharing in the success you help create. Our commitment to development ensures you can Own Your Growth through learning opportunities, career advancement programs, and a collaborative culture that values innovation and teamwork.

At Restek, our core values—We Care, Better Every Day, Respect for All, and Win Together—are at the heart of everything we do. We care deeply about our employee-owners, our customers, and the communities we serve around the world. We strive to be better every day by fostering personal and professional growth while delivering solutions that drive positive global change. We value respect for all, creating a workplace where every voice matters and diverse perspectives drive innovation. And we believe we win together, celebrating shared success as a 100% employee-owned company.

We are an equal opportunity employer, considering applicants without regard to race, ethnicity, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, religion, military or veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Restek provides reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act and applicable laws.

If you’re ready to join a team that lives its values and empowers you to Own Your Future, we’d love to hear your story. Apply today.

Applying for a job at PUMA is easy. Simply click APPLY ONLINE and follow the steps to upload your application.

  

**Your mission**
----------------

Club Assembly

* Provide strategic operational leadership and direction for Manufacturing facilities in North America

* Responsible for all aspects of Club Assembly operation, including Stock and Custom.

* Set, track and monitor Club Assembly operation budget. Work closely with Finance to ensure that the monthly budgets are met.

* Work closely with Sourcing, Program Management and Product Development teams to ensure all assembly process can meet output and quality requirements for the business.

* Establishes, implements, and reports on metrics for measuring operational performance.
  

Production Planning

* Manage production planners to ensure Club assembly operations are building appropriate clubs to meet sales needs.

* Work closely with Warehouse team to ensure proper components are staged for club assembly in a timely manner.

* Manage Custom Assembly plant to meet KPI to meet “Customer Happy” core value.
  

Custom Club Planning

* Creates, establishes, and maintains business processes for managing the custom business from order taking to product shipment
Oversees team who are the liaison between Customer Service, Sales Support Representatives, and the field on Custom Club business  

Leadership & Team Management

* This role will focus on the Cobra Golf operation, including Club Assembly, Global Quality and production planning for golf club categories.
* Implement a culture of “Continuous Improvements”, striving to get better each day. Find process improvement opportunities to drive efficiencies.
* Leads the Operations team in executing best practices and measuring performance through agreed upon Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).
* Proactively develop others within the Cobra operation organization through sharing of best demonstrated processes and knowledge transference.

**Your talent**
---------------

* 10+ years materials management/procurement experience with at least 7 years management experience
* Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain or an equivalent combination of education and experience
* Experience and a solid understanding of ERP systems in a manufacturing and distribution environment; advanced capability in balancing procurement, inventory management, and customer satisfaction within the ERP system settings
* Relationship quality: communication, listening, diplomacy
* Superior analytical skills with demonstrated expertise in MS Excel
* Must have excellent problem-solving skills
* Must be able to work in a fast-paced complex manufacturing environment.
* Exceptional technical aptitude: ability to quickly learn new systems
* Strong relationship-building skills
